title: Myocardial Work Analysis: A Novel Echocardiographic Approach for Early Detection of Myocardial Fibrosis in Pediatric Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy With Preserved LVEF-A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background While myocardial work (MW) indices have shown diagnostic and prognostic value in various cardiovascular diseases, their role in detecting myocardial fibrosis in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) remains unexplored. This prospective study investigates MW's potential for early identification of fibrosis in pediatric DMD patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. Methods In this large prospective cohort, we enrolled 242 genetically confirmed DMD males (aged 6-18 years) with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% by cardiac magnetic resonance and 54 age-matched controls. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment included global work index, global constructive work, global wasted work, and global work efficiency analysis. Myocardial fibrosis was assessed via late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance at baseline at 1-year follow-up. Results Patients with DMD demonstrated significantly impaired MW indices versus controls (global work index, 1371.4±225.84 versus 1598.04±207.01 mm Hg%; global work efficiency, median 94.67% [Q1-Q3, 93.00-96.00] versus 95.33% [94.30-96.33]; global constructive work, 1630.34±246.37 versus 1900.22±195.84 mm Hg%; global wasted work, median 67.67 [Q1-Q3, 50.17-86.25] versus 59.00 [48.00-73.00] mm Hg%; all P <0.01). Notably, MW abnormalities preceded global longitudinal strain reduction, with significant differences even in patients with DMD with normal global longitudinal strain (≥18%). Global work efficiency showed moderate diagnostic accuracy for baseline late gadolinium enhancement (area under the curve, 0.618) and was associated with subsequent late gadolinium enhancement development in exploratory longitudinal analysis (area under the curve, 0.798; cutoff of 95.85%), providing complementary information beyond conventional echocardiographic parameters. Conclusions This large-scale prospective study suggests that MW analysis, particularly global work efficiency, might be useful for early detection of cardiac dysfunction and might be associated with short-term fibrosis in patients with DMD and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. However, given the limited number of progression events, this finding should be interpreted cautiously.

Background

This prospective study investigates MW's potential for early identification of fibrosis in pediatric DMD patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction.

Methods

In this large prospective cohort, we enrolled 242 genetically confirmed DMD males (aged 6-18 years) with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% by cardiac magnetic resonance and 54 age-matched controls. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment included global work index, global constructive work, global wasted work, and global work efficiency analysis. Myocardial fibrosis was assessed via late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance at baseline at 1-year follow-up.

Results

Patients with DMD demonstrated significantly impaired MW indices versus controls (global work index, 1371.4±225.84 versus 1598.04±207.01 mm Hg%; global work efficiency, median 94.67% [Q1-Q3, 93.00-96.00] versus 95.33% [94.30-96.33]; global constructive work, 1630.34±246.37 versus 1900.22±195.84 mm Hg%; global wasted work, median 67.67 [Q1-Q3, 50.17-86.25] versus 59.00 [48.00-73.00] mm Hg%; all P<0.01). Conclusions

This large-scale prospective study suggests that MW analysis, particularly global work efficiency, might be useful for early detection of cardiac dysfunction and might be associated with short-term fibrosis in patients with DMD and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. title: Prognostic Value of Left Ventricular Kinetic Energy Assessed by 4D Flow CMR in Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Alterations in left ventricular intracavitary hemodynamics can occur early in the course of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). However, the association between 4-dimensional (4D) flow cardiac magnetic resonance parameters and adverse outcomes in patients with DCM remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance parameters can predict adverse outcomes in patients with DCM. Methods In this multicenter prospective cohort study, 675 adult patients with DCM (mean age, 56 years; 399 men) from 3 medical centers and 80 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance. Left ventricular flow components and kinetic energy parameters were quantified. The primary end point was a composite of heart failure events, including heart failure-related death, unplanned heart failure hospitalization, or cardiac transplantation. Results During a median follow-up of 42 months, 58 patients (8.6%) experienced the primary end point. Compared with controls, patients with DCM exhibited reduced peak systolic kinetic energy normalized to EDV (KEi EDV ) and peak E-wave KEi EDV ; these differences were more pronounced in those who developed the primary end point. In univariable Cox regression, direct flow, residual volume, peak systolic KEi EDV , and peak E-wave KEi EDV were significant predictors of the primary end point (all P <0.05). After adjustment for left ventricular ejection fraction, NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide), extracellular volume fraction, extent of late gadolinium enhancement, peak systolic KEi EDV (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.28-0.53]), and peak E-wave KEi EDV (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.26-0.48]) remained independently associated with the primary end point (both P <0.001). Furthermore, these 2 kinetic energy parameters provided incremental prognostic value beyond clinical markers and conventional imaging markers for predicting the primary end point. Conclusions In patients with DCM, decreased peak systolic KEi EDV and peak E-wave KEi EDV , as measured by 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance, are independently associated with poor prognosis and provide incremental prognostic value for risk stratification beyond clinical and conventional imaging markers. Registration URL:https://clinicaltrials.gov/; Unique Identifier: NCT07527715.

title: Myocardial Responses to Eplontersen in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: The CARDIO-TTRansform CMR study.
abstract: Background Transthyretin-lowering therapies target the underlying cause of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), but their effects on myocardial amyloid burden and cardiac remodelling remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated the myocardial effects of sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen using serial multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR). Methods This CMR study was a pre-specified, international, prospective study embedded within the randomized, placebo-controlled phase 3 CARDIO-TTRansform trial. Participants underwent CMR at baseline and planned assessments at weeks 25, 49, 97, and 140. The primary imaging analysis evaluated longitudinal changes in CMR parameters using mixed models for repeated measures. Myocardial amyloid regression and progression were defined as ≥5 percentage-point decreases and increases in extracellular volume (ECV), respectively. All other patients were considered stable. Results We enrolled 120 participants with baseline and ≥1 follow-up CMR assessment (eplontersen, n=58; placebo, n=62; mean age, 76.7±6.5 years; 95% male; baseline stabilizer, 12.5%). At week 140 eplontersen resulted in lower ECV, compared with placebo (least-squares mean difference [95% CI], -6.7 percentage points [ -8.7 to -4.7]; P<0.001) and lower native T1 ( -25.9ms [-41.7 to -10.2 ]; P=0.002) and left ventricular mass (-19.1g [-28.0 to -10.2]; P<0.001). Eplontersen also increased left ventricular ejection fraction (+5.1% [1.8-8.3]; P=0.002), right ventricular ejection fraction (+4.6% [0.6-8.7]; P=0.03), and left ventricular global longitudinal, circumferential, and radial strain and right ventricular longitudinal strain (all P<0.05), compared to placebo. At week-140, myocardial amyloid regression occurred in 12.5% receiving eplontersen versus 0% receiving placebo, whereas progression occurred in 12.5% versus 76%, respectively. Conclusions Sustained transthyretin suppression with eplontersen resulted in substantially lower myocardial ECV and favorable changes in cardiac structure, biventricular systolic function, and myocardial deformation compared with placebo in a cohort of patients mostly not on background stabilizer at baseline. These findings provide randomized evidence that lowering circulating transthyretin modifies myocardial disease progression in ATTR-CM and support serial multiparametric CMR for characterizing myocardial treatment response.

abstract: Background Predicting recurrent ischemic stroke (RIS) in patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation remains a clinical challenge, as traditional risk scores such as CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc (congestive heart failure, hypertension, age ≥75 years, diabetes, previous stroke or transient ischemic attack, vascular disease, age 65 to 74 years, and sex category) often fail to account for the mechanistic insights provided by brain imaging. We aimed to evaluate the comprehensive role of neuroimaging parameters in identifying residual RIS risk and to determine their incremental value over clinical scoring systems. Methods In this nationwide, multicenter, prospective cohort study (East Asian Ischemic Stroke Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Study, Part II [EAST-AF]), we enrolled 2270 patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation from 14 stroke centers. We performed hierarchical profiling of magnetic resonance imaging parameters, including acute and chronic infarction characteristics and cerebral small vessel disease markers. Two-year cumulative incidences and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were estimated using cause-specific hazard models. Results During a median follow-up of 431 days, 123 patients experienced RIS (2-year cumulative incidence, 5.6%). The 2-year cumulative incidence of RIS was significantly higher in patients with chronic nonlacunar infarction (7.3% versus 4.6%; aHR, 1.50 [95% CI, 1.01-2.23]) and lacunes (9.0% versus 4.7%; aHR, 1.91 [95% CI, 1.28-2.86]). Mechanistically, lacunes in medullary artery territories, indicative of embolic sources, significantly increased RIS risk (aHR, 2.65 [95% CI, 1.56-4.49]), whereas those in deep perforator territories did not (aHR, 1.54 [95% CI, 0.94-2.53]). Notably, adding these neuroimaging markers to the CHA 2 DS 2 -VASc score significantly improved the model's discriminative ability, increasing the C statistic from 0.53 to 0.63 ( P <0.001). Conclusions Comprehensive neuroimaging profiling, particularly focusing on embolic-pattern markers such as chronic infarctions and medullary lacunes, is essential for identifying high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation who may require intensified secondary prevention. Our findings suggest that imaging-based risk stratification provides critical prognostic information beyond conventional clinical scores.

We aimed to evaluate the comprehensive role of neuroimaging parameters in identifying residual RIS risk and to determine their incremental value over clinical scoring systems.

Methods

In this nationwide, multicenter, prospective cohort study (East Asian Ischemic Stroke Patients With Atrial Fibrillation Study, Part II [EAST-AF]), we enrolled 2270 patients with acute ischemic stroke and atrial fibrillation from 14 stroke centers. We performed hierarchical profiling of magnetic resonance imaging parameters, including acute and chronic infarction characteristics and cerebral small vessel disease markers. Two-year cumulative incidences and adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs) were estimated using cause-specific hazard models.

Results

During a median follow-up of 431 days, 123 patients experienced RIS (2-year cumulative incidence, 5.6%). The 2-year cumulative incidence of RIS was significantly higher in patients with chronic nonlacunar infarction (7.3% versus 4.6%; aHR, 1.50 [95% CI, 1.01-2.23]) and lacunes (9.0% versus 4.7%; aHR, 1.91 [95% CI, 1.28-2.86]). Mechanistically, lacunes in medullary artery territories, indicative of embolic sources, significantly increased RIS risk (aHR, 2.65 [95% CI, 1.56-4.49]), whereas those in deep perforator territories did not (aHR, 1.54 [95% CI, 0.94-2.53]). Notably, adding these neuroimaging markers to the CHA2DS2-VASc score significantly improved the model's discriminative ability, increasing the C statistic from 0.53 to 0.63 (P<0.001).

Conclusions

Comprehensive neuroimaging profiling, particularly focusing on embolic-pattern markers such as chronic infarctions and medullary lacunes, is essential for identifying high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation who may require intensified secondary prevention. title: Risk Stratification and Outcomes of Right Atrial Phasic Function in Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy: A Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Study.
abstract: Background Advanced arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy is associated with a high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias (MVA) and end-stage heart failure (HF). However, the prognostic role of right atrial (RA) mechanics, as quantified by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), remains largely unexplored. Methods Consecutive patients with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy undergoing CMR between 2014 and 2021 were retrospectively included. Demographics, clinical history, and strain parameters were collected. The primary clinical end points were end-stage HF and MVA. Results A total of 316 patients (mean age 38±15 years; 66.1% men) were included. Over a median follow-up of 5.3 years, 49 developed end-stage HF and 103 experienced MVA outcomes. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Gray models showed that impaired RA reservoir strain was an independent predictor of end-stage HF (hazard ratio [HR] 0.92, 95% CI 0.89-0.96, P <0.001) and MVA outcomes (subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR) 0.98, 95% CI 0.96-0.99, P =0.025), with added prognostic value beyond clinical and imaging variables, improving the C-statistic to 0.84 and 0.70, respectively. Kaplan-Meier survival curves indicated that RA reservoir strain <18.6% was associated with higher end-stage HF risk, consistent across subgroups regardless of left ventricular involvement (both log-rank P <0.05). The association between RA reservoir strain <23.0% and MVA was significant in the overall cohort ( P <0.001) and in patients without left ventricular involvement ( P =0.002), but not in those with left ventricular involvement ( P =0.08). Conclusions Lower cardiac magnetic resonance-derived RA reservoir strain was independently associated with end-stage HF and MVA in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional risk markers. These findings support RA mechanics as a potential complementary component of multichamber CMR risk assessment, pending external validation.

title: Standardized Ultrafast Transcranial Ultrasound Acquisition in Acute Stroke: The HYPER-AI-SCAN Pilot Study With Exploratory Artificial Intelligence Analysis.
abstract: Background Intracerebral hemorrhage requires rapid mechanism-specific treatment, yet early stroke triage relies on clinical severity scales that do not reliably distinguish hemorrhage from ischemic stroke. We assessed the feasibility of a standardized ultrafast transcranial ultrasound protocol designed to support subsequent artificial intelligence (AI)-based intracerebral hemorrhage detection. Methods HYPER-AI-SCAN (Hyper-Acute AI-Assisted Sonographic Cerebral Hemorrhage Assessment Network) was a single-center prospective feasibility study with embedded exploratory AI analysis. Between March and December 2025, 102 adults with acute computed tomography (CT)-confirmed stroke were prospectively enrolled according to trained operator availability. Primary feasibility outcomes were protocol completion, operator-rated adequate transtemporal windows, and acquisition time. In patients with retrievable paired baseline CT, exploratory AI analyses compared CT-only, ultrasound-only, and cross-modal CT-guided ultrasound models using patient-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, and specificity. Results Two patients were excluded after acquisition because insonation depth was <19 cm, yielding 100 evaluable patients (33 intracerebral hemorrhage; 67 ischemic stroke). The protocol was completed in all evaluable patients; adequate transtemporal windows were identified in 87%, and median acquisition time was 22 seconds (interquartile range, 13-31). Paired baseline CT images were available in 91 patients. Mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.86 (SD, 0.07) for the CT-only model, 0.85 (SD, 0.14) for the ultrasound-only model, and 0.92 (SD, 0.07) for the cross-modal model. Conclusions Standardized ultrafast transcranial ultrasound acquisition was feasible at the bedside in acute stroke and generated brief cine-loops suitable for exploratory AI development. Multicenter external validation is required before diagnostic or triage application. Registration information Clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT07319013.

title: Association Between Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Background The prognostic utility of the hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) in posterior circulation stroke is undefined. We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion. Methods This post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION (Endovascular Treatment for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion)/ATTENTION-IA (Intra-Arterial Tenecteplase After Successful Endovascular Recanalisation in Patients With Acute Posterior Circulation Arterial Occlusion) trials included patients with posterior circulation occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had baseline computed tomography perfusion. HIR (Tmax>10 s/ Tmax>6 s volume) was analyzed. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days was the primary outcome. Results Among 139 patients, higher HIR (per 0.1 increment) was independently associated with lower odds of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.643 [95% CI, 0.422-0.979]; P =0.039). However, its discriminative ability was the modest (area under the curve, 0.617 [95% CI, 0.521-0.712]). The established anterior circulation cutoff (HIR<0.4) did not predict outcomes ( P =0.115). Conclusions Elevated HIR is independently associated with worse 90-day outcomes after posterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy, but its overall prognostic utility is limited, and the anterior circulation threshold (0.4) could not be validated in this underpowered analysis, highlighting circulation-specific pathophysiological differences.

title: Processing strategies for improving cortical thickness correspondence between low-field and high-field MRI in young people.
abstract: Portable low-field MRI systems are a promising complement to conventional high-field systems, enabling broader access to MRI. However, correspondence in cortical thickness estimates between low- and high-field MRI in young people remains limited despite its importance for neurodevelopment and psychopathology. To evaluate how multiple low-field image processing approaches improve cortical thickness correspondence with high-field MRI in a large sample of young individuals, we collected T1-weighted (T1w) and T2-weighted (T2w) data using both low-field (64 mT) and high-field (3T) MRI within 1 week of each other from a community sample of young people. We applied deep learning-based super-resolution methods (SynthSR v1 and SynthSR v2) followed by recon-all, or other reconstruction methods (recon-all-clinical and recon-any), to low-field data acquired across multiple sequences (T1w and T2w) and orientations (axial, coronal, sagittal, and multi-orientation average), with and without resampling and/or co-registration. We assessed global, lobar, and regional cortical thickness correspondence with 3T MRI measures based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas using Pearson and intraclass correlations. We compared pipelines using Steiger's Z -tests and Fisher's Z -tests. A total of 150 individuals (mean age, 18.63 ± 5.07 years; 80 female) were included. We observed the highest global correspondence with recon-all-clinical applied to coronal T1w images ( r = 0.40, p FDR = 3.02e-05), which significantly exceeded the best global correspondence in our previous study (Fisher's Z = 1.99, p = 0.047). originalAbstract: Portable low-field MRI systems are a promising complement to conventional high-field systems, enabling broader access to MRI. title: SRNR: Deep learning-based MRI super-resolution using noisy high-resolution reference data.
abstract: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) techniques offer a powerful tool to enhance the spatial resolution of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) without increasing scan time. However, most supervised SR methods rely on high-resolution, high-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) reference data for training, which are difficult to acquire in many clinical settings, such as in time-constrained pediatric imaging. Inspired by the Noise2Noise principle, we propose SRNR, a new training paradigm that enables supervised SR using noisy high-resolution images as references. SRNR was systematically evaluated on both pediatric and adult simulated data across different noise levels of the reference data. SRNR generated super-resolved image volumes with high similarity to the high-resolution references (PSNR: 32.5-35.2 dB) and improved downstream image analysis performance, including tissue segmentation (white matter Dice coefficient: 0.951-0.960) and cortical surface reconstruction (cortical thickness absolute difference: 0.200-0.255 mm). Furthermore, SRNR was shown to be effective on clinically acquired pediatric brain MRI data, achieving improvements consistent with those observed in the simulated experiments. These results demonstrate that SRNR substantially reduces reliance on clean, high-SNR training data and enables effective SR under clinically realistic acquisition constraints, thereby improving the feasibility of deploying deep learning-based SR in pediatric MRI and related applications.

title: The MTL200: A surface-based, probabilistic atlas of the medial temporal lobe.
abstract: The human medial temporal lobe (MTL) includes a number of cortical regions surrounding the hippocampus implicated in long-term memory and high-level perception, including entorhinal cortex (ERC), perirhinal cortex (PRC), parahippocampal cortex (PHC), and the medial aspect of temporopolar cortex (TPC). A critical prerequisite to studying the function of these areas is to define their anatomical boundaries. While several atlases or segmentations methods for automated boundary definition exist, they have limitations: (1) they are derived from small sample sizes; (2) most do not include TPC; and (3) they are volumetric rather than surface-based and are therefore not straightforward to use for surface-based analysis of MRI data. Here we present the MTL200: a surface-based, probabilistic atlas of MTL regions ERC, PRC, PHC, and TPC. The atlas is derived from hand drawings of regions based on gross anatomical features corresponding to cytoarchitectonic boundaries, using anatomical MRI data from 200 human participants. This work provides a valuable tool for researchers studying the anatomy and function of MTL regions, particularly the poorly characterized area TPC.

title: WHITE-Net: White matter HyperIntensities Tissue Extraction using deep learning network.
abstract: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are a hallmark of cerebral small vessel disease, a highly prevalent condition in aging, making their accurate detection in large-scale magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies critically important. Currently available semi-automated and automated segmentation methods are frequently limited by sensitivity to variations in imaging conditions and computational constraints, restricting their applicability across diverse acquisition settings. We present WHITE-Net, a deep learning-based framework for automated WMH segmentation built on a 3D ResUNet architecture and trained on multisite MRI data encompassing substantial variability in scanner vendors, acquisition protocols, spatial resolution, and image characteristics. Evaluated across three independent datasets-BrainLaus, ADNI, and WMH Challenge, WHITE-Net achieves high segmentation accuracy and ranks among the top-performing methods across datasets, enabling a comprehensive assessment of generalizability in varied imaging environments. WHITE-Net maintains stable performance in a wide spectrum of lesion loads and demonstrates a favorable balance between precision and recall, effectively limiting false positive detections-a common limitation of existing approaches. Beyond accuracy, WHITE-Net requires no parameter tuning and offers fast inference times, making it well suited for deployment in large-scale neuroimaging studies. The obtained results highlight the value of training on diverse multisite data for improving generalizability and position WHITE-Net as a reliable, scalable tool for automated WMH segmentation in computational anatomy research.

title: MAMBAxBrain: A multi-task neural framework linking brain functional dynamics to individual fingerprints, cognitive and disease states.
abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) contains rich individual, cognitive, and pathological information, yet no universal model exists for multi-task modeling of these dimensions. Here, we introduce MAMBAxBrain, a multi-task neural framework that integrates Mamba architecture with functional connectivity analysis to jointly model the temporal dynamics and spatial coordination of neural activity. MAMBAxBrain achieves high accuracy across four distinct fMRI objectives, including brain fingerprinting, cognitive task decoding, reaction time prediction, and schizophrenia classification, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art methods with robust cross-session generalization. Interpretability analyses show that each task engages distinct, biologically plausible circuitry: from higher-order association cortex for identity to subcortical-motor loops for reaction time and disrupted control-sensory connectivity for schizophrenia. These findings inform a longstanding debate: rather than operating through wholly separate or entirely shared systems, the brain preferentially recruits task-specific circuits while retaining common representational structure across functions.

title: Volumetric Quantification of Retinal Ischemic Perivascular Lesions (RIPLs) in Coronary Artery Disease.
abstract: Purpose Retinal ischemic perivascular lesions (RIPLs) have been reported as correlates of several systemic conditions. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, number, area, and volume of RIPLs and to evaluate their association with coronary artery disease (CAD) using a contemporary imaged coronary angiography (CA) cohort. Methods CA patients were imaged using an SS-OCTA device during the same visit. Structural volumes comprising 500 B-scans were pixel-wise annotated by three graders. RIPLs were quantified by presence, count, area and volume for the first time. CAD severity was assessed using the Gensini score (GS). Associations between RIPL metrics and CAD were analyzed using generalized estimating equation models. Multivariable and age and sex adjusted models were calculated. Multiple testing corrections were applied to primary analyses. Results RIPLs were detected in 38.0% of eyes. In models with the Gensini score (GS) as outcome, RIPL metrics showed weak and inconsistent trends and were not statistically significant, especially after adjustment. The GS showed no significant associations with RIPL presence (β = 0.132, P = 0.102), area (β = 0.173, P = 0.093), count (β = 0.023, P = 0.165), or volume (β = 0.240, P = 0.085) either. Cardiovascular risk factors were not independently associated with RIPL metrics. Those negative findings remained consistent in sensitivity analyses using the SYNTAX II and SCORE2. Conclusions In this contemporary coronary angiography cohort with high-density OCT imaging, RIPL burden was not significantly associated with CAD and no robust or proportional association with CAD severity was found. In this work, no other disease specific associations could be established.

title: Detection of Abnormalities in the RPE in Long-Chain 3-Hydroxyacyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency Chorioretinopathy Using Optical Coherence Tomography-Derived Optical Attenuation Coefficients.
abstract: Purpose To detect abnormalities in the RPE in long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (LCHADD) chorioretinopathy, a novel method using optical attenuation coefficients (OACs) was used to enhance the contrast between regions with high and low attenuation. Methods LCHADD patients were scanned over the central macula using two commercial optical coherence tomography (OCT) devices. Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) imaging was performed during the same visit to detect RPE abnormalities based on lipofuscin distribution. OAC was derived from OCT data. En face OAC of the retina (internal limiting membrane to Bruch's membrane [BM]), en face OCT of the RPE (16 µm above the BM to the BM), and corresponding FAF images were compared to evaluate the ability of the OAC to detect RPE abnormalities. Pairwise comparisons were performed across all LCHADD stages, along with correlations with traditional clinical metrics including LCHADD severity, best-corrected visual acuity, and plasma acylcarnitines. Results Forty-three eyes from 22 LCHADD patients were evaluated and categorized into 6 stages. OAC images of the retina revealed RPE defects consistent with FAF, with clearer and more detailed visualization of RPE disruption. Compared with OCT images, OAC images facilitated visualization of pathological changes and provided a better visual comparison between the preserved and degenerated RPE at advanced stages. The mean retinal OAC decreased significantly (P < 0.001) with disease progression and differed significantly across disease stages (all P ≤ 0.002), showing strong correlations with traditional clinical metrics. Conclusions OCT-based OAC is a promising tool for both the quantitative and qualitative assessment of RPE abnormalities in LCHADD chorioretinopathy.

title: The Emory Optic Nerve Head Atlas: Using 3D Anatomical Mapping to Study Optic Neuropathies With an Initial Focus on Glaucoma.
abstract: Purpose To develop the first three-dimensional (3D) optic nerve head (ONH) atlas using artificial intelligence (AI)-based registration and evaluate its use in (1) atlas-referenced retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) analysis for glaucoma diagnosis, and (2) strain-based assessment of glaucoma severity. Methods Large-scale optical coherence tomography (OCT) datasets were registered using REFLECTIVITY-generated tissue segmentations. A healthy atlas (n = 460) and glaucoma atlases for mild (n = 852), moderate (n = 640), and severe (n = 546) disease were built using an AI-driven algorithm incorporating intensity- and structure-based constraints with deformation regularization. Atlas quality was evaluated using interlayer contrast and agreement between warped scans and the template. Atlas-referenced RNFL thickness was obtained by defining Bruch's membrane opening (BMO)-centered reference points along a fixed 3-mm-diameter circle in atlas space and mapping these locations to each subject using the registration deformation field. These measurements were then compared with conventional subject-specific RNFL measurements. Effective strain relative to each atlas was computed by morphing subjects to the atlas template. Atlas-referenced RNFL profiles were evaluated for healthy versus early glaucoma classification, and strain volumes were used for multiclass glaucoma severity classification. Results The healthy atlas captured normative ONH anatomy, and the glaucoma atlases showed stage-dependent changes (cup deepening, prelaminar thinning, rim narrowing). Registration accuracy was high (normalized cross-correlation = 0.86 ± 0.05; Dice coefficient = 0.90 ± 0.02), with strong inter-layer contrast (0.40 ± 0.03). Atlas-referenced RNFL thickness improved separation between healthy and mild glaucoma (Cohen's d = 0.77 vs. 0.72). Classification using atlas-referenced profiles outperformed conventional fixed-circle measurements (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.91 ± 0.02 vs. 0.89 ± 0.02; DeLong P = 0.003). Mean effective strain differed significantly across severity groups (ANOVA P < 0.05), and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on strain maps achieved strong classification (AUC = 0.79). Conclusions The ONH atlas provides a population-derived structural reference enabling anatomically consistent RNFL mapping and 3D characterization of structural deviation. Atlas-referenced RNFL measurements improved diagnostic discrimination, and geometric strain maps demonstrated the potential of the framework for characterizing disease-associated anatomical differences.

These measurements were then compared with conventional subject-specific RNFL measurements. Effective strain relative to each atlas was computed by morphing subjects to the atlas template. Atlas-referenced RNFL profiles were evaluated for healthy versus early glaucoma classification, and strain volumes were used for multiclass glaucoma severity classification.

Results

The healthy atlas captured normative ONH anatomy, and the glaucoma atlases showed stage-dependent changes (cup deepening, prelaminar thinning, rim narrowing). Registration accuracy was high (normalized cross-correlation = 0.86 ± 0.05; Dice coefficient = 0.90 ± 0.02), with strong inter-layer contrast (0.40 ± 0.03). Atlas-referenced RNFL thickness improved separation between healthy and mild glaucoma (Cohen's d = 0.77 vs. 0.72). Classification using atlas-referenced profiles outperformed conventional fixed-circle measurements (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.91 ± 0.02 vs. 0.89 ± 0.02; DeLong P = 0.003). Mean effective strain differed significantly across severity groups (ANOVA P < 0.05), and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on strain maps achieved strong classification (AUC = 0.79).

Conclusions

The ONH atlas provides a population-derived structural reference enabling anatomically consistent RNFL mapping and 3D characterization of structural deviation. Atlas-referenced RNFL measurements improved diagnostic discrimination, and geometric strain maps demonstrated the potential of the framework for characterizing disease-associated anatomical differences.

title: Phenotypic Variability in Individuals With Genotype-Matched EYS- and USH2A-Associated Autosomal-Recessive Retinitis Pigmentosa.
abstract: Purpose Variable expressivity is well recognized in autosomal-dominant inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) but is increasingly observed and less well defined in recessive IRDs. Despite the traditional view of recessive IRDs as monogenic disorders with high penetrance, phenotypic differences among individuals sharing identical biallelic variants suggest additional disease modifiers. We quantified genotype-phenotype concordance in EYS- and USH2A-associated retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and characterized phenotypic variability among individuals with identical primary genotypes. Methods Participants underwent standardized ophthalmic assessment with multimodal imaging. Longitudinal ellipsoid zone (EZ) widths were measured from optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans obtained ≥12 months apart. Baseline EZ width and age at OCT assessment were compared among individuals sharing identical primary genotypes. Genotype-matched comparisons in which younger individuals demonstrated smaller EZ widths than older counterparts were classified as age-discordant structural comparisons. Results Ninety patients (41 EYS, 49 USH2A) were included. Recurrent variants EYS c.6416G>A (p.Cys2139Tyr) and USH2A c.2802T>G (p.Cys934Trp) were identified in 46% and 35% of probands, respectively. Females showed greater baseline EZ preservation, although differences were not statistically significant. Marked variability was observed within matched genotypes. Several genotype-matched comparisons demonstrated age-discordant structural variability, including younger individuals with substantially smaller EZ widths than older genotype-matched counterparts. In EYS-associated disease, the largest discordant comparison demonstrated 85.4% less EZ preservation in the younger individuals despite younger age, and the corresponding value in USH2A-associated disease was 81.8%. Intrafamilial discordance further supported the possibility of modifying influences beyond the primary genotype. Conclusions Disease severity varied substantially among individuals sharing identical primary genotypes, supporting contributions from additional genetic or environmental modifiers. Translational relevance Recognition of variability within recessive IRDs has implications for prognosis, trial stratification, and interpretation of treatment response beyond genotype alone.

title: Vascular Retinomics Decodes Panvascular Progression: A Retinal Polyvascular Disease Risk Index.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate whether color fundus photograph-derived vascular retinomics predicts progression from single vascular disease to polyvascular disease. Methods This prospective cohort study included UK Biobank participants with baseline single vascular disease and eligible color fundus photographs. Progression was defined as incident involvement of a previously unaffected coronary, cerebrovascular, or peripheral arterial bed. After LASSO-Cox and Boruta feature selection, eight survival-learning algorithms were compared. The best-performing model was refitted to derive the Retinal Polyvascular Disease Risk Index (RPVDRI). Performance was evaluated in the testing cohort and benchmarked against conventional clinical factors and SMART2. Results Among 2592 participants, 334 progressed during a median follow-up of 11.39 years. A 25-feature vascular retinomic panel was retained, and a gradient boosting machine performed best. In the testing cohort, the RPVDRI showed a graded association with progression after multivariable adjustment (highest vs. lowest tertile: hazard ratio, 1.97; 95% confidence interval, 1.03-3.74; P = 0.040; P for trend = 0.029). The RPVDRI achieved 3-, 5-, and 10-year areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.636, 0.716, and 0.628, respectively. Adding the RPVDRI to conventional clinical factors improved 5-year AUC by 0.113 (P = 0.002), whereas the corresponding improvement beyond SMART2 was 0.037 (P = 0.466). Shapley additive explanations linked predictions to multidomain features and co-attribution. Conclusions The RPVDRI was independently associated with polyvascular disease progression and may complement clinical risk assessment in secondary prevention, particularly in scalable or opportunistic settings where comprehensive clinical information is limited. Translational relevance Fundus-derived vascular retinomics may support precision secondary prevention by noninvasively stratifying residual polyvascular progression risk.

title: Static Perimetry-OCT Topographical Overlay Findings in the RUSH2A Study.
abstract: Purpose Ellipsoid zone (EZ) loss on optical coherence tomography (OCT) correlates with diminished sensitivity on static perimetry (SP). We explore a topographical overlay analysis in USH2A-related retinitis pigmentosa (RP) to develop novel endpoints of structural and functional change. Methods Subjects (N = 105) had SP (3× baseline; once annually for 4 years) and annual OCT. B-scans were segmented to outline the EZ. Overlays used visual field modeling and analysis (VFMA) software to superimpose the hill of vision (HOV) onto the en face infrared (IR) fundus image with EZ contours segmented from OCT volume scans. EZ border and three ribbons straddling the EZ border were ray cast onto the HOV. The HOV volume, HOV slope, mean sensitivity (MS), and peak sensitivity were measured. Mixed effect models were used to estimate change rates. Results Significant decrease over 4 years was found in all measures within the EZ, except slope and peak sensitivity. MS decreased for all ribbons, with outer ribbons showing greater progression than inner ribbons. Inner ribbons had larger decreases in volume and slope than outer ribbons. Conclusions SP-OCT overlay analysis showed faster loss of sensitivity outside the EZ margin. The widest ribbon outside the EZ showed greatest progression, suggesting more rapid vision loss occurring distal to the EZ margin. Slope progressed most within the widest inner ribbon, which could mean that slope change is a precursor to EZ loss. Translational relevance This research explores novel endpoints and concepts to characterize the disease progression in USH2A-related RP using imaging and functional overlay techniques.

title: Amblyopic Eyes Show Reduced Retinal Vessel Density Compared to Fellow Eyes Using Widefield Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography Angiography.
abstract: Purpose Amblyopia has traditionally been considered a purely functional disorder without an organic correlate. Recent optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) studies, however, revealed alterations in the central retinal vasculature of amblyopic eyes. This prospective, monocentric study is the first, to our knowledge, to employ widefield swept-source OCTA (WF-SS-OCTA) for a quantitative assessment of the retinal and choroidal vasculature extending to the periphery, comparing amblyopic eyes with healthy fellow eyes. Methods Patients with unilateral amblyopia were recruited at Münster University Hospital and underwent WF-SS-OCTA imaging. The superficial capillary plexus (SCP) and choroid were analyzed using AngioTool software. Results A total of 102 eyes from 51 patients were included. In amblyopic eyes, the SCP demonstrated significantly lower vessel pixel density (VPD) (P = 0.01), fewer junctions (P = 0.01), shorter vessel length (total and average, both P < 0.01), and increased lacunarity (P < 0.01) compared to fellow eyes, whereas the number of end points did not differ significantly (P = 0.10). Subgroup analysis showed that moderate amblyopia was associated with significantly lower VPD, fewer junctions, and shorter total vessel lengths compared to mild amblyopia, with no significant differences in end points or lacunarity. No significant differences were observed in choroidal vascular parameters (all P > 0.46). Conclusions These findings support an organic correlate of amblyopia, characterized by a less dense superficial retinal vascular network, possibly reflecting postnatal regression or impaired retinal vascular development due to inadequate visual stimulation in early childhood. Translational relevance WF-SS-OCTA may provide an objective imaging biomarker for amblyopia severity.

title: Cerebellar and frontal lobe alterations in pulmonary hypertension implicate an inflammatory lung vascular/brain axis.
abstract: Connections between vascular and neurocognitive diseases are emerging but remain poorly defined. Cognitive impairment is increasingly recognized in pulmonary hypertension (PH), a disease traditionally viewed as limited to the heart and lungs. Given that inflammation is shared by PH and neurodegenerative diseases, we investigated its role in driving brain and cognitive deficits in PH. Using structural and functional MRI data from UK Biobank (N = 248 PH) and a prospective validation cohort, we identified reduced cerebellar white matter volume, thinner frontal gyri, and weakened cerebellar-frontal connectivity in patients with PH but not in other heart or lung diseases. These changes were accompanied by worsened executive function and processing speed. Olink proteomics and targeted genomics linked inflammatory plasma proteins and a PH-associated nuclear receptor coactivator 7 (NCOA7) single nucleotide polymorphism, rs11154337, to these deficits. PH cerebellum showed increased microglial activation and white matter derangement. In PH mice, Ncoa7 deficiency worsened cerebellar inflammation and atrophy. Microglial functional assays, cerebellar single-nucleus RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic analyses further implicated Ncoa7-dependent lysosomal, inflammatory, and cell-specific mechanisms of cerebellar pathobiology. These findings identify NCOA7-linked inflammatory dysfunction in the cerebellar-frontal axis in PH, redefining this disease with neurologic consequences and thus offering neural targets for diagnostic, prognostic, and therapeutic development.

title: Quality, clinical utility, and economic implications of routine intraoperative cholangiography during laparoscopic cholecystectomy: A standardised audit study.
abstract: BackgroundLaparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is the standard treatment for gallstone disease, but routine intraoperative cholangiography (IOC) remains controversial regarding image quality and downstream resource use. This audit evaluated routine IOC performance, quality, clinical utility, and financial impact.MethodsA retrospective audit assessed 279 consecutive adults undergoing LC with attempted IOC (January-December 2024). Image quality was assessed using a novel 12-point checklist applied independently by three trained readers, with consultant adjudication of disagreements. Outcomes included IOC success, image quality, clinical findings, subsequent interventions, and costs.ResultsBiliary cannulation succeeded in 93.2% (260 out of 279) of cases, but only 66.92% (174 out of 260) met the pre-specified high-quality threshold (≥6 of 8 core parameters). Visualisation was lowest for the cystic duct junction and right sectoral ducts. Sixteen significant findings were identified, including 11 choledocholithiasis cases. No bile duct injuries occurred. Equivocal IOC-driven imaging led to 14 postoperative magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatographies, of which only five demonstrated pathology. Low-yield downstream imaging and prolonged admissions generated £11,800 in excess costs.ConclusionsRoutine IOC is feasible, but variable technical quality drives unnecessary downstream investigations and healthcare expenditure. Standardised reporting using a 12-point checklist can improve quality and resource utilisation.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Multimodal Neuroimaging, Eye-Tracking, and Related Biomarkers in Schizophrenia: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveSchizophrenia is a complex neuropsychiatric disorder for which accurate and objective diagnostic tools remain limited. The objective of this meta-analysis was to examine advances in neuroimaging, machine learning, and eye tracking to determine whether the use of multimodal methods involving these techniques is promising in the early identification of schizophrenia.MethodsA systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the Google Scholar database was conducted for studies published between 2015 and 2025. Eligible studies reported quantitative diagnostic performance of structural MRI, functional MRI, diffusion imaging, eye-tracking, or their multimodal use in identifying schizophrenia. Eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Data extraction included accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC in terms of predictive accuracy. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using the available study-level estimates. Heterogeneity, subgroup analyses, and publication bias were assessed where supported by the available data.ResultsAcross included studies, classification performance varied across multimodal approaches and study methodologies. Multimodal neuroimaging studies reported classification accuracies ranging from 75.05% to 90.83%, while eye-tracking studies reported accuracies ranging from 78.8% to 96.37%. Sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were not consistently reported across studies; therefore, unsupported pooled estimates for these metrics were not retained. Heterogeneity estimates and subgroup findings were interpreted cautiously because of the small number of included studies, and publication bias could not be excluded definitively.ConclusionMultimodal neuroimaging and eye-tracking approaches show promising discrimination between individuals with schizophrenia and healthy controls. However, current evidence does not support their routine clinical use. These approaches may have an auxiliary role in clinical assessment, but large-scale, multicentre studies with independent external validation are required before clinical implementation.

title: EXPRESS: Brain Age Gap from Non-Contrast CT Is Independently Associated with Functional Outcome after Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BackgroundOutcomes after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) vary beyond lesion burden and clinical severity, suggesting a role for baseline structural brain vulnerability. We evaluated whether brain age gap (BrainAGE) derived from routine non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) is associated with functional outcome after AIS.MethodsWe analyzed 1,173 AIS patients from a prospective multicenter cohort. A deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline NCCT to minimize lesion-related confounding. BrainAGE was defined as predicted minus chronological age. The primary outcome was 90-day functional status, assessed using proportional odds regression adjusted for age, sex, baseline stroke severity, early ischemic changes, and reperfusion therapy.ResultsBrainAGE was higher in AIS patients than in controls (+3.1 ± 9.1 years; p<0.001). Higher BrainAGE was associated with worse functional outcome after adjustment for age, sex, and other clinical predictors (POR 1.091 per 5 years; 95% CI 1.023-1.162; p=0.008). BrainAGE improved model fit but modestly improved discrimination.ConclusionsBrainAGE from routine NCCT provided modest incremental prognostic information beyond age and conventional clinical predictors. These findings support CT-based BrainAGE as a marker of brain health complementary to established prognostic factors. Whether BrainAGE improves patient-level risk stratification or clinical decision-making requires independent external validation and prospective evaluation.

title: Interpretable machine learning for bone mineral density regression via computed tomography radiomics: A retrospective cross-sectional study.
abstract: ObjectiveThe limited interpretability and generalizability of machine learning models for bone mineral density regression hinder their clinical application. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a machine learning model for lumbar bone mineral density regression using computed tomography radiomics and to assess its interpretability through Shapley Additive exPlanations analysis.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center, cross-sectional study, 150 patients who underwent routine abdominal computed tomography and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry scans between April 2018 and November 2023 were included. Lumbar vertebral bodies were segmented using 3D-slicer, followed by radiomics feature extraction. Machine learning models, including EXtreme gradient boosting, light gradient boosting machine, gradient boosting decision tree, support vector machine, and random forest, were used for bone mineral density regression and T-score classification. Shapley Additive exPlanations analysis was used to assess global and local interpretability.ResultsThe EXtreme gradient boosting algorithm showed the best performance for bone mineral density regression, with an R 2 of 0.80, mean absolute error of 0.07, mean squared error of 0.01, and Pearson's r of 0.90. The T-score classification achieved a weighted average precision, recall, and F1 score of 0.75, 0.71, and 0.72, respectively. Shapley Additive exPlanations analysis provided global insights into feature contributions and local interpretability for individual samples.ConclusionsThis study introduced an interpretable method using routine computed tomography scans and the EXtreme gradient boosting algorithm to predict lumbar bone mineral density. The top radiomic features identified through Shapley Additive exPlanations analysis, such as Coarseness and RunEntropy, may contribute to accurate bone mineral density prediction.

title: Subapical Upper-Calyx Access in Prone Mini-PCNL: Comparative Outcomes and Dynamic Renal Mobility.
abstract: To describe subapical fornix puncture for upper-calyx access in mini-percutaneous nephrolithotomy, compare it with conventional apical puncture, and explore whether intrinsic renal mobility may compensate for the initial tract angle after access establishment. This retrospective cohort study included 288 patients who underwent upper-calyx PCNL from May 2020 to November 2024 (subapical, n = 150; apical, n = 138). The puncture approach was nonrandomly selected. Subapical puncture was defined as fornical access with the puncture trajectory shifted approximately 30° caudally from the apical fornix line. Outcomes were compared between groups. In a consecutive 30-patient subapical ultrasound subset, renal surface-to-skin displacement during nephroscope pivoting was measured; an exploratory post hoc mobility-stratified analysis used the subset median as the cutoff. Operative time was shorter with subapical than apical puncture (77.98 ± 13.35 vs. 88.19 ± 14.56 minutes; P < 0.001). Hemoglobin decrease, hospital stay, postoperative pain, and early CT clearance were similar. Pleural, hepatic, or splenic injury occurred only after apical puncture (0 vs. 5 [3.6%]; P = 0.024). In an exploratory subset of 30 subapical cases, mean intraoperative renal displacement was 1.35 ± 0.45 cm. Subapical puncture was associated with shorter operative time without compromising early CT clearance or increasing bleeding. Access-related pleural or visceral injuries were observed only in the apical group. These findings are consistent with a stage-dependent view of renal mobility: movement that can complicate access creation may become advantageous after tract establishment and help expand the working range of a subapical upper-calyx tract.

title: Prior-guided residual implicit neural representation for limited-angle CT reconstruction.
abstract: Incomplete angular measurements in computed tomography (CT) cause severe directional ambiguity and streak artifacts, limiting clinical applicability. Existing prior-guided implicit neural representation methods typically use a single network to preserve prior information and reconstruct the target image, which may compromise reliable prior structures. We propose a prior-guided residual implicit neural representation framework for limited-angle CT reconstruction. The target image is modeled as the sum of a frozen prior representation and a trainable residual representation. The frozen prior network preserves stable anatomical structures learned from a previous scan, while the residual network recovers target-specific changes and compensates for artifacts using measured limited-angle projections. A periodically updated missing-view projection loss is further introduced to constrain the unmeasured angular range. The residual network is optimized using measured-view data fidelity, estimated missing-view consistency, and residual sparsity regularization. Under the 120 ° setting, it achieved the highest PSNR and SSIM on all three simulated slices and improved mean PSNR by approximately 1.29 dB over NeRP. This advantage remained as the acquisition range decreased from 150 ° to 60 ° . The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively suppresses limited-angle artifacts and preserves reliable details compared with competing algorithms.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled medical image analysis in photon-counting CT: A review of segmentation, detection, classification and characterization, and automated quantification.
abstract: BackgroundPhoton-counting computed tomography (PCCT) provides finely sampled morphological images and energy-resolved products that may alter the behavior of artificial-intelligence models developed for conventional CT.ObjectiveThis review synthesizes downstream AI applications in PCCT and determines which study designs support claims of feasibility, transfer, spatial or spectral contribution, scanner advantage, and clinical utility.MethodsA structured narrative search identified original studies evaluating segmentation, detection, classification and characterization, and automated quantification on reconstructed PCCT images. Each analytical configuration was coded by task, effective input, model provenance, development or adaptation strategy, reference standard, comparator, testing independence, and evidence maturity.ResultsTechnical feasibility has been demonstrated across all four tasks. Established conventional-domain models often retained useful local performance on PCCT, while PCCT-native studies explored virtual monoenergetic images, threshold or energy-bin images, material maps, and multienergy feature spaces. However, small cohorts, repeated non-independent observations, incomplete external testing, limited matched PCCT-EID comparisons, and scarce spatial or spectral ablations restrict causal attribution. Prospective workflow evidence remains uncommon.ConclusionsPCCT creates important opportunities for AI-enabled image analysis, but availability of high-resolution or energy-resolved information does not establish its contribution to performance. Claims should be aligned with the comparator, ablation, reference standard, and validation design required to support them.

title: Evaluation of wedge-induced photoneutron dose during 15 MV 3D conformal rectal radiotherapy using TLD600/TLD700 pairs.
abstract: BackgroundLinear accelerators are widely used in radiotherapy. However, photoneutron production may occur during high energy photon radiotherapy. Neutrons have a high radiation weighting factor.PurposeTo compare the thermal neutron sensitive TLD responses with and without wedge use during simulated rectal radiotherapy using TLD600/700 pairs.MethodsTLD pairs were placed in the target (rectal region), bladder, and right femur regions of an anthropomorphic Rando phantom for simulated rectal radiotherapy. Computed tomography images were acquired and transferred to the Prowess treatment planning system (TPS). Wedge and non-wedge plans were created using 15 MV photons at a treatment dose of 2 Gy. Plans were delivered using a Siemens Artiste™ linear accelerator. TLDs were read using a Harshaw system, and Am-Be calibrated neutron sensitive responses were expressed in mSv/Gy. Wedge/non-wedge response ratios were also calculated.ResultsAm-Be calibrated values for wedge versus non-wedge plans were 0.37 vs. 0.19 mSv/Gy for the target, 0.43 vs. 0.17 mSv/Gy for the bladder, and 0.51 vs. 0.22 mSv/Gy for the right femur, corresponding to wedge/non-wedge ratios of 1.95, 2.53, and 2.32, respectively.ConclusionsNeutron sensitive TLD responses were higher for the wedge plan than for the non-wedge plan at the same measurement positions.

title: Brain Structural Changes in Blast-Exposed Special Operations Forces Soldiers.
abstract: Special Operations Forces (SOF) soldiers experience frequent low-level occupational blast exposure and mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), but the cumulative effects of these exposures on long-term neurological health remain poorly understood. The purpose of this longitudinal cohort study was to investigate associations between occupational blast exposure and brain structural change in SOF soldiers and to determine whether mTBI sustained between assessments moderated these associations. Male SOF soldiers ( n = 88) underwent T1- and T2-weighted magnetic resonance imaging at two timepoints. Volumetric segmentation was performed using FreeSurfer. Main outcomes were percent change in global brain tissue volumes, including cerebral cortex, cerebral white matter, lateral ventricles, subcortical gray matter, and cerebellar cortex. Exposure was quantified as months between Time 1 and Time 2, used as a proxy for cumulative occupational blast exposure during time in a high-tempo operational unit. The number of self-reported mTBIs sustained between timepoints was categorized as 0, 1-2, or 3 or more injuries. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate. Greater occupational blast exposure predicted increased lateral ventricle percent change ( F 1,86 = 9.86; B = 0.126%; R 2 = 0.103; p = 0.002; p -adjusted = 0.012) and decreased cerebellar cortex percent change ( F 1,86 = 5.72; B = -0.074%; R 2 = 0.062; p = 0.019; p -adjusted = 0.047). Between-visit mTBI did not significantly moderate these associations. In this cohort of SOF soldiers, greater cumulative occupational blast exposure was associated with lateral ventricular expansion and cerebellar cortex volume loss. The rate of ventricular expansion observed in this study is atypical compared with expected change in healthy adults and may represent an early structural marker of blast-related brain vulnerability. Cerebellar cortex volume loss may reflect regional susceptibility to blast-related injury. Identifying brain structural changes associated with occupational blast exposure may help inform exposure-monitoring strategies and targeted interventions to preserve warfighter brain health and readiness.

The number of self-reported mTBIs sustained between timepoints was categorized as 0, 1-2, or 3 or more injuries. The Benjamini-Hochberg procedure was applied to control the false discovery rate. Greater occupational blast exposure predicted increased lateral ventricle percent change (F1,86 = 9.86; B = 0.126%; R2 = 0.103; p = 0.002; p-adjusted = 0.012) and decreased cerebellar cortex percent change (F1,86 = 5.72; B = -0.074%; R2 = 0.062; p = 0.019; p-adjusted = 0.047). Between-visit mTBI did not significantly moderate these associations. In this cohort of SOF soldiers, greater cumulative occupational blast exposure was associated with lateral ventricular expansion and cerebellar cortex volume loss. The rate of ventricular expansion observed in this study is atypical compared with expected change in healthy adults and may represent an early structural marker of blast-related brain vulnerability. Cerebellar cortex volume loss may reflect regional susceptibility to blast-related injury. Identifying brain structural changes associated with occupational blast exposure may help inform exposure-monitoring strategies and targeted interventions to preserve warfighter brain health and readiness.

title: The Association of MRI-Derived Tissue Bridge Morphometrics with Baseline Impairment and Recovery in Traumatic Spinal Cord Injury: A Subanalysis of the RISCIS Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Early prognostic biomarkers are essential to optimize treatment and trial design in spinal cord injury (SCI). The Riluzole in SCI Study (RISCIS), a multicenter randomized controlled trial, provided evidence on secondary analyses that riluzole improved functional recovery in acute cervical SCI. The current analysis uses magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess lesion and tissue bridge morphometrics against baseline impairment, functional recovery, and treatment response in RISCIS participants. In this preplanned ambispective subanalysis, 24 participants underwent T2-weighted MRI for acute cervical SCI together with neurological and functional assessments to 12 months. A subset also had diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), used to extract fractional anisotropy (FA) values. Segmentation with the Spinal Cord Toolbox (v7.2) gave ventral, dorsal, and total tissue-bridge widths and lesion volume and length. Associations with American Spinal Injury Association Impairment Scale (AIS) grade, upper extremity motor score (UEMS) and total motor score (TMS), lower extremity motor score (LEMS), light touch and pinprick sensory scores, Spinal Cord Independence Measure (SCIM), and Short Form-36 (SF-36) domains at baseline and follow-up were analyzed with regression models adjusted for age and sex. Overall recovery across TMS, SCIM, and SF-36 Physical Component Summary was analyzed with an O'Brien-style global statistical test (GST). Interactions tested whether bridge metrics modified riluzole's effect. At baseline, greater ventral ( β = 9.65, p = 0.017) and total ( β = 6.16, p = 0.021) tissue-bridge widths were associated with higher TMS, and ventral width with higher UEMS ( β = 6.61, p = 0.010). Larger dorsal (odds ratio [OR] = 21.92, p = 0.013), ventral (OR = 4.91, p = 0.049), and total (OR = 3.70, p = 0.019) bridges corresponded to less severe baseline AIS grade. Pinprick scores increased with ventral ( β = 26.56, p = 0.020) and total ( β = 17.50, p = 0.023) bridge width, and light touch scores increased with total bridge width ( β = 16.22, p = 0.045). No imaging metric was associated with LEMS. These individual-metric associations were nominally significant but did not survive correction. In GST analyses, larger ventral ( T = 4.63, p = 0.012, p '= 0.048) and total ( T = 4.30, p = 0.019, p '=0.048) bridges predicted greater overall recovery; both remained significant after correction and were stable across sensitivity analyses. Ventral and total bridge width showed nominally significant interactions with riluzole treatment for upper-limb motor recovery. Exploratory DTI findings were inconclusive and sensitive to individual observations: both the FA-recovery association and the observation of poor outcome despite a preserved tissue bridge rested on a single participant. Overall, we found that midsagittal tissue-bridge width measured ∼72 h after injury from standard-of-care T2-weighted MRI was associated with baseline injury severity and multidomain functional recovery, at a timepoint substantially earlier than the 1 month at which tissue bridges have previously been quantified. Because edema may obscure lesion margins this early, acute bridge widths may underestimate spared tissue resolvable later. The treatment-interaction observation is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective confirmation. These findings support MRI-derived tissue bridges as candidate biomarkers for prognostication and enrichment of neuroprotective trials in SCI.

title: A deep learning approach for brain tumor classification using hybrid efficient net and inception networks in MRI images.
abstract: BackgroundA brain tumor is a medical pathology, whereas biomedical imaging is a key element used to visualize the condition. Brain tumor classification is an essential imaging task for early pinpointing and treatment. Accurate and timely tumor characterization supports appropriate treatment planning, prognosis assessment and better patient outcomes.ObjectiveThis paper aims to develop an efficient hybrid deep learning model for early detection of brain tumors from MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) images.MethodsTo classify tumors, this work proposes a hybrid EfficientNet B7 and Inception V4 (ENETV4) network. The Inception network interprets spatial features for improving classification accuracy, while the EfficientNet B7 framework increases the computational efficiency to maintain high feature extraction ability. A unified feature is created by concatenating the retrieved features from the two models. To improve classification performance, a Figshare dataset comprising glioma, meningioma and pituitary tumor MRI images was used. Optimized hyperparameters enhanced generalization across the 70:20:10 train-test-validation split of the multi-sequence MRI dataset.ResultsThe proposed hybrid ENETV4 networks achieved 98.53% accuracy using an independent dataset, outperforming existing methods when evaluated on the dataset. These results accurately differentiate various kinds of tumors. This paper compares the hybrid ENETV4 model with the traditional models, reaffirming that the hybrid ENETV4 method enables effective classification of brain tumors from medical images, helping clinicians select suitable treatment strategies.ConclusionThe proposed hybrid methods provide accurate tumor classification in an early stage, supporting timely clinical decisions and treatment planning.

title: AI- assisted compressed sensing for accelerated 1.5T shoulder MRI.
abstract: BackgroundShoulder MRI has relatively long acquisition times. The clinical performance of AI-assisted compressed sensing (ACS) acceleration levels in 1.5-T shoulder MRI remains unclear.ObjectiveTo compare the acquisition time, image quality, and diagnostic agreement of three clinical shoulder MRI protocols using parallel imaging (PI), ACS4, and ACS8 at 1.5 T.Materials and MethodsProspectively, 158 patients with shoulder discomfort underwent three scanning protocols-the conventional Parallel imaging (PI) protocol, the ACS with a nominal acceleration factor of 4 (ACS4), and the ACS with a nominal acceleration factor of 8 (ACS8), covering four common sequences. Acquisition time, quantitative image quality parameters including True SNR, Relative SNR, Relative CNR, and edge rising distance (ERD), subjective image quality scores from three radiologists, and diagnostic agreement in an exploratory subgroup of 25 patients were assessed.ResultsACS4 and ACS8 reduce the total acquisition time by approximately 29% and 45%, respectively, compared with the PI protocol while maintaining comparable image quality across evaluated sequences. ACS8 generally demonstrated higher quantitative Relative SNR/CNR values in several tissues and sequences, whereas ACS4 achieved the highest True SNR and subjective image quality scores. ERD differences were not statistically significant, and diagnostic agreement was generally high across protocols.ConclusionACS protocols reduced acquisition time in 1.5-T shoulder MRI, although ACS8 compromised subjective image quality. ACS4 offered a more favorable balance between scanning efficiency and image quality.

title: Riesz-Quincunx WaVnet Chaotic Rime Attention Encoder and ensemble convolutional neural networks for remote brain tumor diagnosis.
abstract: BackgroundAccurate classification and segmentation of brain tumors from medical images are essential for reliable diagnosis and treatment planning. However, variations in image quality, noise, and tumor characteristics can complicate automated analysis.ObjectiveThis study aims to develop a deep learning framework for the accurate classification and segmentation of brain tumors by integrating an ensemble convolutional neural network (CNN) with the Riesz-Quincunx WaVnet Chaotic Rime Attention Encoder.MethodsThe proposed framework incorporates image preprocessing techniques to enhance contrast, reduce noise, and improve image quality. The ensemble CNN is integrated with the Riesz-Quincunx WaVnet Chaotic Rime Attention Encoder to strengthen feature extraction and representation. The framework is designed to identify brain abnormalities and classify tumor subregions, including necrotic tumor cores, enhancing tumors, peritumoral edematous areas, and non-enhancing tumor cores. Furthermore, a Flask-based web application is developed to facilitate remote access and support clinical collaboration.ResultsThe proposed framework is designed to improve brain tumor classification and segmentation by combining ensemble learning with enhanced feature representation. However, quantitative performance metrics are required to substantiate its diagnostic accuracy, segmentation performance, and superiority over existing methods.ConclusionThe proposed deep learning framework integrates image preprocessing, ensemble CNN classification, and attention-based feature extraction to support automated brain tumor analysis. Its Flask-based deployment offers potential for remote accessibility and telemedicine applications, supporting medical specialists in diagnostic decision-making. Further validation using quantitative performance metrics and independent clinical datasets is necessary to establish its clinical reliability.

title: A review of medical image segmentation research based on bibliometrics.
abstract: BackgroundMedical image segmentation is a fundamental step in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning, and its research landscape has expanded rapidly with the advancement of artificial intelligence. A systematic bibliometric overview of this field is therefore needed to clarify its intellectual structure and emerging trends.ObjectiveTo provide a comprehensive bibliometric overview of the global research landscape, developmental trends, collaboration networks, and emerging hotspots in the field of medical image segmentation over the past decade.MethodsA bibliometric analysis was performed on 21,437 publications related to medical image segmentation, indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection from 2016 to 2025. The analysis systematically examined publication outputs, country-level contributions, author collaboration networks, journal distributions, and keyword co-occurrence patterns.ResultsThe annual publication count increased remarkably from 25 in 2016 to 5,207 in 2025. China contributed the largest share with 11,556 publications, followed by the United States (3,272) and India (1,924). Core researchers formed stable intra-team collaborations, though inter-team cooperation remained limited. Keyword and citation analyses identified deep learning, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Transformers, U-Net, and their variants as dominant methodological themes. Case studies on skin and lung segmentation revealed differential research attention and international collaboration patterns across anatomical targets. A historical trajectory analysis showed methodological evolution from traditional image processing to fully convolutional networks and U-Net, and subsequently to hybrid architectures integrating attention mechanisms and Transformers.ConclusionMedical image segmentation has experienced substantial growth, driven by deep learning innovations. Future research may increasingly focus on multimodal foundation models capable of generalizable segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios. This bibliometric review offers researchers a valuable reference for understanding the intellectual structure and frontiers of the field.

title: Attention-enhanced TransUNet for ultrasound liver parenchyma segmentation toward assessment of schistosomiasis-associated liver disease.
abstract: BackgroundSchistosomiasis-associated liver disease is the most common clinical form of chronic schistosomiasis. Chronic hepatic schistosomiasis is mainly manifested as liver fibrosis, cirrhosis and other liver dysfunction, and even induces liver cancer in the late stage. Ultrasound is widely used for the diagnosis of schistosomiasis-associated liver disease, grading of liver fibrosis, and assessment of of therapeutic effects.ObjectiveThe study aims to detect and segment the ultrasound liver parenchyma with high accuracy.MethodsWe propose an attention-enhanced TransUNet that improves skip-connection feature transfer by integrating axial attention with residual connections, while retaining the Vision Transformer module for global context modeling. Axial attention re-weights features along spatial axes to emphasize direction-sensitive structures such as liver boundaries, and residual refinement mitigates information degradation during multi-scale fusion. We compared the proposed method against UNet and the original TransUNet using Dice, IoU, and Sensitivity. Ablation studies further demonstrated that combining axial attention with residual connection outperformed axial attention alone.ResultsThe proposed model achieved a satisfactory performance in the delineation of the ultrasound liver parenchyma region, with a Dice coefficient of 0.965, an IoU of 0.931 and a Sensitivity value of 0.970.ConclusionThe results support the feasibility of the attention-enhanced TransUNet model as an upstream module for accurate ultrasound image analysis in schistosomiasis-associated liver disease such as fibrosis staging and cirrhosis.

title: Data expansion and local tuning: A strategy for effective clinical deployment of AI in pulmonary nodule screening.
abstract: BackgroundThe clinical performance of pulmonary nodule screening systems may be influenced by training data size and differences in imaging characteristics across institutions. Improving model performance and cross-center adaptability is important for clinical deployment.ObjectiveTo investigate the effects of data expansion and localized fine-tuning on a pulmonary nodule screening system (PNSS) and evaluate its clinical utility for pulmonary nodule detection and classification.MethodsLung CT scans from Weifang People's Hospital and Shandong Provincial Hospital were retrospectively analyzed to assess PNSS performance with different training dataset sizes. Localized fine-tuning was further applied to improve cross-center adaptability. A prospective study at Weifang People's Hospital compared PNSS with experienced radiologists in routine clinical practice.ResultsData expansion increased detection sensitivity from 0.7703 to 0.9428 and classification accuracy from 0.7029 to 0.9486, with performance gains gradually approaching saturation. Localized fine-tuning improved cross-center diagnostic accuracy from 53.57% to 85.36% and sensitivity from 0.5495 to 0.8736. In the prospective evaluation, PNSS achieved a sensitivity of 0.9302 for malignant nodules, 13.95 percentage points higher than radiologists. Overall diagnostic accuracy was 0.92 compared with 0.85 for radiologists. PNSS required only 34 s per case, nearly eight times faster than radiologist review.ConclusionData expansion and localized fine-tuning significantly improved PNSS performance, adaptability, and efficiency, supporting its clinical application in pulmonary nodule screening and early lung cancer detection.
