title: Transcript-based circulating tumor and cancer stem cell detection in inflammatory breast cancer: a six-year prospective evaluation of assay yield and prognostic performance
abstract: Abstract Inflammatory breast cancer (IBC) is a rare and aggressive presentation for which no validated blood-based monitoring tool exists, and the tumor emboli that define its biology have motivated interest in circulating tumor cell (CTC) assays. We prospectively evaluated a transcript-based platform combining epithelial CTC markers (MUC1, HER2, GA733-2) and cancer stem cell (CSC)-associated markers (TWIST, AKT, PI3K, ALDH1) in patients with stage III breast cancer enrolled from 2013 to 2020, comparing 54 patients with IBC against 23 with non-IBC disease across 222 quality-controlled serial samples. Using the manufacturer-defined positivity thresholds, 14% of samples were CTC-positive and 29% CSC-positive. No marker distinguished IBC from non-IBC at baseline: GA733-2 was positive in 7 of 54 IBC versus 1 of 23 non-IBC patients (p = 0.42), and the composite positive categories did not differ (p = 0.71 for CTC, p = 0.11 for CSC). HER2 and TWIST transcripts were undetectable at threshold in all 77 patients. Among 44 IBC patients evaluable for event-free survival over a median 65 months of follow-up, neither baseline CTC positivity (log-rank p = 0.10) nor CSC positivity (p = 0.55) stratified outcome. Threshold sensitivity analysis showed that detectable signal clustered an order of magnitude below the positivity cutoffs, so that no threshold produced both an adequate positivity rate and outcome discrimination. Positivity at any draw during follow-up, and an additive classification combining both marker classes, likewise showed no association with outcome. Benchmarked against a tumor-informed ctDNA assay evaluated by our group in the same disease setting, the two platforms showed near-identical sample-level positivity (29% versus 27%) and technical QC performance, yet only ctDNA positivity tracked disease trajectory and preceded radiographic relapse. These findings indicate that transcript-based CTC and CSC detection, as implemented here, does not provide clinically actionable risk stratification in IBC, and they support prioritizing sequencing-based circulating tumor DNA and next-generation CTC platforms for minimal residual disease monitoring in this population.

title: Impact of Body Mass Index Percentile on Ultrasound Diagnostic Performance and Operative Duration in Pediatric Appendicitis
abstract: Abstract Purpose Childhood obesity may affect diagnostic imaging and operative duration in pediatric appendicitis. We evaluated associations between body mass index (BMI) percentile, imaging outcomes, and operative duration. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of children younger than 18 years with surgically confirmed appendicitis presenting to a tertiary pediatric emergency department from 2010–2023. BMI percentiles were categorized using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention standards. Outcomes included computed tomography (CT) utilization, nondiagnostic ultrasound, and operative duration. Multivariable models adjusted for age, sex, and calendar year. Results Of 2,275 children, 2,011 had valid BMI classification. CT utilization did not differ across BMI categories (p = 0.143). Nondiagnostic ultrasound was more frequent in children with Overweight and Obesity, although categorical differences were not significant (p = 0.079). Increasing BMI percentile was independently associated with nondiagnostic ultrasound (aOR 1.07 per 10-percentile increase, 95% CI 1.02–1.13; p = 0.011) and longer operative duration (β = 0.69 minutes per 10-percentile increase, 95% CI 0.07–1.32; p = 0.030), but not CT utilization (p = 0.146). Conclusion Increasing BMI percentile was associated with nondiagnostic ultrasound and modestly longer operative duration, but not CT utilization.

title: Lesion-Grounded Content-Based Retrieval of CT Findings Using Foundation Model Patch Embeddings for Case Review
abstract: Abstract Background Computed tomography (CT) education benefits from prior examinations containing related localized findings. Whole-volume retrieval can be driven by global anatomy or unrelated findings, while database-specific retrieval models limit reuse. This study evaluates whether patch tokens from a frozen volumetric CT foundation encoder can support a reusable lesion-grounded retrieval framework without task-specific retrieval fine-tuning. Methods Spatial patch tokens were pooled into lesion representations linked to their parent examination, annotation, and source finding text. ReXGroundingCT served as the demonstration benchmark. The primary evaluation used FlexiCT-3D to search 14,359 reference lesions with 407 public-validation queries from 50 CT examinations. Exact masks, bounding boxes, and loose boxes tested sensitivity to query-region precision. Retrieval was evaluated against ontology-based relevance, analytic chance expectations, and annotation-informed descriptor controls. Results For exact-mask queries, exact-subcategory Recall@1 was 0.484, more than three times the analytic chance expectation of 0.154, while Recall@10 was 0.848 versus 0.729. Bounding-box and loose-box queries gave Recall@10 of 0.840 and 0.821, respectively, but less precise query regions lowered early-rank performance. Under both box policies, embedding retrieval outperformed the descriptor-only control. Conclusions A reusable lesion-retrieval layer can be built from frozen volumetric foundation features without task-specific retrieval training. The layer retains links to source finding text without using text for ranking and can organize compatible medical-image databases into lesion-centered ranked lists and localized review panels for educational case comparison.

title: Hybrid U-Net Model with Transformer-Enhanced Skip Connections for Abdominal Organ Segmentation in Laparoscopic Images
abstract: Abstract The organ Segmentation in surgical images plays a crucial role in computer-assisted diagnosis and robotic surgeries, yet it faces challenges like class imbalance, occlusions, and computational constraints. In order to overcome these challenges, we propose an architecture which uses asymmetric multi-scale transformer along with the attention-gated skip connections in U-Net Model to efficiently segment abdominal organs. Our proposed architecture allows efficient extraction of local features and modelling of global contexts. We also propose a hybrid loss function by combining Lovasz-Softmax loss and sparse categorical cross-entropy loss, which helps in overcoming class imbalance in the training process and improving performance on the minor classes. Our proposed method attains a mean precision of 0.9667, mean recall of 0.9432, mean dice of 0.9522, mean IoU of 0.9150, and mean HD95 of 0.4704 on all 13 classes of the CholecSeg8k dataset, which makes it better than the state-of-the-art techniques.

title: Dynamic digital radiography–derived low signal area ratio for assessing emphysema and associated pulmonary vascular changes in COPD
abstract: Abstract Emphysema in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) destroys alveolar walls together with the alveolar capillary bed, yet unenhanced computed tomography (CT) quantifies parenchymal change rather than perfusion. Dynamic digital radiography (DDR) generates perfusion-related maps from cardiac-synchronised changes in radiographic lung density without contrast material. In 40 prospectively enrolled patients with clinically stable COPD who underwent breath-hold DDR, inspiratory high-resolution CT and pulmonary function testing, we quantified a low signal area (LSA) ratio by histogram-based segmentation of DDR perfusion maps. The LSA ratio correlated with the percentage low attenuation volume at CT ( r s = 0.692), forced expiratory volume in 1 s ( r s = − 0.553) and diffusing capacity ( r s = − 0.436). Absolute pulmonary vessel volume showed no association with the LSA ratio, whereas vessel volume normalised to lung volume did ( r s = − 0.556); this association persisted after adjustment for emphysema extent (partial r = − 0.324) and for lung volume (partial r = − 0.517), although its confidence interval approached zero. When both CT measures were considered simultaneously, the LSA ratio was more strongly related to emphysema extent than to vessel volume. The LSA ratio therefore reflects emphysematous destruction predominantly, with an additional pulmonary vascular component that requires confirmation.

title: CT-Derived Leaflet Sizing Discrepancy Is Associated With Valve-Related Events After Aortic Valve Neocuspidization
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate leaflet sizing is essential for aortic valve neocuspidization (AVNeo), yet objective anatomical references for selecting leaflet size remain limited. We investigated whether the discrepancy between a patient-specific computed tomography (CT)-derived anatomical reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size was associated with valve-related events after AVNeo and assessed the reproducibility of the CT-derived measurements. Methods We retrospectively investigated 32 consecutive patients who underwent AVNeo with preoperative ECG-gated CT. A CT-derived reference leaflet size was geometrically estimated from the intercommissural distance. Sizing discrepancy was defined as the difference between the CT-derived reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size, with maximum Δ representing the largest discrepancy among the three cusps. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed using independent measurements by a radiologic technologist, an experienced cardiovascular surgeon, and a cardiovascular surgery trainee. Associations with valve-related events were assessed using Cox proportional hazards and receiver operating characteristic analyses, and interobserver reliability was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients. Results During a median follow-up of 23 months, valve-related events occurred in eight patients. Greater maximum Δ was associated with valve-related events (hazard ratio, 1.39 per 1-mm increase; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.09–1.78; P = 0.004). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis identified 4.9 mm as the optimal cutoff (area under the curve [AUC], 0.818; 95% CI, 0.647–0.989), and patients with maximum Δ ≥ 4.9 mm had lower valve-related event-free survival (log-rank P = 0.020). Interobserver reliability was moderate to good, with intraclass correlation coefficients of 0.726 (95% CI, 0.339–0.881), 0.703 (95% CI, 0.231–0.879), and 0.832 (95% CI, 0.516–0.932) for the right coronary, left coronary, and noncoronary cusps, respectively. Observer-specific AUCs for maximum Δ were 0.776 for the radiologic technologist, 0.818 for the experienced cardiovascular surgeon, and 0.667 for the cardiovascular surgery trainee. Conclusions Greater discrepancy between the CT-derived anatomical reference and intraoperatively selected leaflet size was associated with subsequent valve-related events after AVNeo. CT-derived measurements showed moderate-to-good interobserver reliability, although discriminatory performance varied among observers. These findings support further investigation of CT-derived anatomical sizing as a patient-specific reference for AVNeo, while highlighting the need for standardized measurement methods and external validation in larger cohorts. Clinical trial registration Not applicable. This study was a retrospective observational study and was not a clinical trial.

title: Development and Validation of an MRI-Based Nomogram for Risk Stratification of Anxiety in Parkinson’s Disease
abstract: Abstract Objective Anxiety, a common and disabling non-motor symptom of Parkinson’s disease (PD), highlights the clinical importance of early identification of PD with anxiety (PDA). This study aimed to develop and internally validate an nomogram that integrates routine clinical indicators and structural MRI radiomic features for early PDA risk stratification. Methods 139 PD patients were retrospectively enrolled and split into training (n = 97) and internal test (n = 42) sets at a 7:3 ratio. 21 clinical variables were collected, and 584 quantitative morphological features were extracted. Mann-Whitney U test, Spearman collinearity elimination and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used to select optimal imaging metrics to calculate a radiomics signature. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified independent clinical predictors. A clinical prediction model and an integrated clinical–radiomics nomogram were constructed, and assessed in terms of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, F1-score, receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration plots and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Elevated UPDRS-III score, cognitive impairment, higher levodopa-benserazide dosage, and 12 MRI features were independent PDA predictors. The combined nomogram outperformed the clinical-only model, achieving an AUC of 0.99, accuracy of 0.93, sensitivity of 1.00, specificity of 0.91 in the test set. Calibration curves confirmed favorable consistency between predicted and actual anxiety risk, while DCA demonstrated sustained net clinical benefit of the integrated nomogram across wide threshold ranges. Conclusion The visualizable clinical-radiomics nomogram enables accurate individualized PDA risk prediction. This non-invasive, bedside-accessible tool assists neurologists in early screening and stratified management of PDA.

title: Thermo-regulatory response of static and dynamic breast thermography as a biomarker of malignancy
abstract: Abstract This study assesses the diagnostic potential of static and dynamic infrared thermography by relating physiological vascular patterns to established indicators of breast malignancy. Mammography remains the principal global screening modality; however, its accuracy declines in women with dense breast tissue [1], and its high cost limits access in developing countries [2]. Although dynamic thermal imaging may improve lesion detection, its clinical implementation in developing settings is constrained by the opacity of artificial intelligence models and the limited availability of high-quality datasets [3]. This paper presents a physiology-based model intended to reduce reliance on extensive training data and thereby facilitate analysis in small patient cohorts. Earlier Virtual Wave Transformation approaches appear to capture dynamic thermal responses but struggle to differentiate metabolic heat from vascular signals. The present study combines dynamic thermal imaging with static infrared imaging. By exploiting the different temporal behaviors of these signals, the model may distinguish increased cancer-related metabolic activity from other thermal patterns. In contrast to black-box deep-learning systems and even explainable AI approaches, this algorithm provides a more interpretable mathematical alternative by decomposing thermal patterns and separating convective vascular heat transport from thermal conductive metabolic signals. Analysis of the temporal variation in each component's amplitude indicates a possible association with patient diagnosis. Whereas conventional AI methods generally require large databases and expensive clinical validation, such as MRI, this approach uses physiological parameters to obtain diagnostic information from smaller samples. This work is a limited pilot study focused on evaluating the mathematical methods; we did not perform detailed statistical analysis.

title: Explainable AI-Based Pulmonary Nodule Classification from Computed Tomography Images with an End-to-End Clinical Decision Support Interface
abstract: Abstract Early and accurate detection of pulmonary nodules in computed tomography (CT) imaging is critical for reducing lung cancer mortality. Although deep learning-based computer-aided detection (CAD) systems have demonstrated promis-ing diagnostic performance, their widespread clinical adoption has been impeded by two persistent limitations: the absence of visual explainability and the lack of deployable end-to-end interfaces that integrate prediction, explanation, and clinical workflow. This paper presents an explainable, end-to-end CAD system for pulmonary nodule classification that addresses both shortcomings. The proposed system employs a transfer-learned ResNet-50 architecture, fine-tuned on 2,372 balanced CT patches extracted from the publicly available LUNA16 dataset. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) is integrated into the inference pipeline to generate per-prediction heatmaps that visually localize the discriminative regions driv-ing each classification decision. The complete system is deployed as a production-grade web application featuring a FastAPI backend and a React frontend, complete with authentication and database persistence. On a held-out test set of 356 samples, the proposed system achieves an accuracy of 90.45%, precision of 90.91%, recall of 89.89%, F1 score of 90.40%, and an AUC-ROC of 0.9615. A confidence-based abstention mechanism returns an “Inconclusive” verdict for predictions below a 60% probability threshold, reducing the risk of unreliable automated decisions. Rather than claiming state-of-the-art raw accuracy, this work’s principal contribution is demonstrating that competitive classification performance, real-time visual explainability, and a fully deployed, browser-accessible clinical interface can be integrated into a single reproducible, open-source system, contributing a practical baseline for future hospital validation studies.

title: Multiparametric CEST MRI–Guided Intranasal Theranostic Liposomes for Quantitative Biodistribution and Response Prediction in Glioblastoma
abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) treatment is limited by the blood-brain-barrier(BBB) and lack of non-invasive methods to track drug delivery and therapeutic response simultaneously. We developed a theranostic strategy utilizing multiparametric chemical exchange saturation transfer(CEST) MRI to guide the nose-to-brain delivery of mucus-penetrating liposomes encapsulating gemcitabine and iohexol(1:1; Gem/Ioh-Lipo). These multiple CEST contrast indicated drug-specific signals (gemcitabine 2.4 ppm, iohexol 4.3 ppm and liposome − 3.5 ppm), demonstrating that > 70% intranasal dose reached the frontal cortex from the olfactory bulb.Importantly, CEST at 4.3 ppm strongly correlated with tumor response(R² > 0.9), indicating the prognostic value of image-guidance. Another CEST contrast (APTw at 3.5 ppm) indicated the tumor response, intranasal Gem/Ioh-Lipo produced an 8.6-fold tumor volume reduction versus drug-free liposomes (P < 0.0001). Controls showed a 55.9% increase in APTw signal in tumor (P < 0.005), indicating increased cellularity and proliferating cells, which were absent in treated animals. This CEST MRI-guided theranostic strategy enables non-invasive, real-time quantification of drug biodistribution and therapeutic efficacy for GBM, enabling precise treatment evaluation.

title: Large asymptomatic gastric duplication cyst presenting as an indeterminate gastrohepatic cystic mass in an adult: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Adult gastric duplication cysts are rare, and their organ of origin can be difficult to determine preoperatively, particularly when large and predominantly exophytic. We report a large, asymptomatic cyst arising from the anterior gastric wall near the lesser curvature and protruding into the gastrohepatic space, whose gastric origin was indeterminate on computed tomography. Case presentation An asymptomatic 27-year-old Han Chinese woman was incidentally found to have an upper abdominal cystic lesion during evaluation at a weight-management clinic. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed an approximately 8-cm, well-circumscribed, nonenhancing cystic mass adjacent to the lesser curvature, but its organ of origin remained unclear. Laparoscopic exploration showed that the lesion arose from the anterior gastric wall near the lesser curvature, with a broad attachment measuring approximately 5 × 5 cm, and was separable from adjacent organs. The cyst ruptured unintentionally during dissection, releasing an estimated 300–400 mL of yellow fluid, which was immediately evacuated. Recovery was uneventful, and computed tomography at approximately 3 months showed no visible residual lesion or re-formed cystic cavity. Conclusions A large, predominantly exophytic gastric duplication cyst may remain asymptomatic and mimic an indeterminate cystic mass in the gastrohepatic region. When imaging is inconclusive, correlation of the operative anatomy with the histopathological findings may support the diagnosis. title: Machine learning implementation for host-based infectious disease diagnostics
abstract: Abstract Host-based diagnostics coupled with machine learning may support faster discrimination of infectious states and reduce unnecessary antimicrobial treatment. We reviewed recent studies that applied machine-learning methods to clinical patient data for pathogen detection, infection classification, or closely related host-response diagnosis. Eligible infection targets included bacterial and viral infections, bacterial-versus-viral classification, and syndrome-based presentations such as sepsis. Malaria was included when evaluated within a mixed febrile cohort. Searches were conducted of four literature databases spanning January 2020 through August 2025. Of 144 retrieved records, 51 passed an initial host-diagnostics screen and 21 articles met the final eligibility criteria. The included articles covered structured clinical variables, gene or molecular-expression measurements, medical imaging, physiological signals, and microscopy. For the quantitative model-class comparison, we extracted 54 evaluations belonging to four machine-learning classes: random forest (23), neural network (17), support vector machine (9), and logistic regression (5). Less frequently evaluated approaches, including gradient boosting, decision trees, naive Bayes, and k-nearest neighbors, were summarized descriptively. Model performance could not be compared directly because input modalities, cohort composition, preprocessing, validation strategies, hyperparameter selection, and reported endpoints varied substantially. Accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were the dominant performance measures. Among the 54 focal-class evaluations, 14 reported accuracy alone, 20 reported AUC alone, and 20 reported both. Only 16 evaluations reported additional measures such as sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, or Matthews correlation coefficient. Imaging studies generally favored neural-network approaches, whereas molecular-expression studies frequently used random forests. However, the evidence did not support a universally optimal model.

title: Quality Assurance of Brachytherapy Treatment Planning Based on Template, Classification, and Segmentation Methods
abstract: Abstract Background and purpose Accurate applicator reconstruction is essential for dose calculation in CT-based brachytherapy. Reconstruction errors—driven by limited CT slice thickness and metal artifacts—can produce clinically relevant dose deviations. We developed a fully automated quality assurance (QA) pipeline that combines deep learning classification and segmentation with high-resolution template registration to verify the geometric accuracy of planned source dwell positions. Materials and methods We retrospectively collected 3,702 treatment plans from 742 gynecological cancer patients. A lightweight 3D convolutional neural network classified applicators into five categories, and an nnU-Net (v2) model segmented the three channels of Fletcher applicators. High-resolution (0.6-mm) template centerlines were registered to 3-mm clinical CT images using a progressive weighted arc-segment Kabsch algorithm. Geometric consistency was quantified with point-to-curve Euclidean distances. Error-detection performance was assessed in a simulation study in which one randomly selected dwell position per plan was displaced by 1, 3, or 5 mm (50 plans per magnitude), with 50 error-free plans as controls. Results The classification model achieved 99.28% accuracy and a weighted F1 score of 0.99. The segmentation model yielded a mean Dice coefficient of 90.7% and a 95% Hausdorff distance of approximately 1 mm. Mean distances between auto-segmented centerlines and the registered template curve ranged from 0.39 to 0.70 mm; mean dwell-point-to-template distances were 0.34–0.51 mm. In the simulation study, specificity was 94.0%; sensitivity was 36.0% for 1-mm displacements and 100% for both 3-mm and 5-mm displacements. Conclusion The proposed pipeline enables automated, high-precision QA of brachytherapy dwell positions and reliably detects displacements of 3 mm or larger, providing an objective tool for clinical treatment-plan verification that mitigates thick-slice artifacts through high-resolution template registration.

title: Screening of Bacillus bacterial strains with capability of degrading T-2 toxin
abstract: Abstract T-2 toxin (T-2) is a toxic fungal metabolite mainly produced by Fusarium species that are known to contaminate food products worldwide, posing serious risks to public health and the economy. Effective control of this toxin is therefore a key objective in food safety. Recent efforts to manage T-2 contamination have focused on utilizing microbes, especially bacterial species from the Bacillus genus, as promising toxin degraders. This study evaluated the in vitro capacity of ten Bacillus strains (BC1–10) in degrading T-2. Three out of ten strains demonstrated T-2 degradation activity, with complete toxin removal achieved within 96 hours under standard culture condition. The major biotransformation product of T-2 was isolated by high-performance liquid chromatography and structurally characterized by nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy as HT-2 toxin. Toxicity assessment in kidney-derived HEK293T cells showed that HT-2 was less toxic than T-2, with EC 50 values of 12.8 and 1.8 nM, respectively. The findings supported the potential application of selected Bacillus strains as functional microbial additives to mitigate T-2 contamination and toxicity.

title: Characterizing the Spatiotemporal Boundaries of Functional Ultrasound for Brain Decoding
abstract: Abstract Functional ultrasound imaging (fUS) measures task-associated changes in cerebral blood volume (CBV) with fine spatial sampling and rapid acquisition, supporting functional mapping and brain-signal decoding. As an indirect measure of neural activity, fUS-CBV signals are shaped by neurovascular coupling and vascular dynamics, which influence the spatial and temporal stimulus information available for decoding. Consequently, the functional distinctions accessible in fUS-CBV signals require characterization under controlled experimental conditions. Here, controlled whisker stimulation in awake, head-fixed mice was used to characterize these decoding-relevant response properties. Whisker identity and number, stimulation duration, and inter-stimulus interval were systematically varied. All-whisker stimulation produced contralaterally dominant responses in the primary somatosensory barrel field and ventral posteromedial thalamic nucleus. Different whisker inputs were associated with distinguishable cortical response distributions, while stimulation involving more whiskers produced broader representative activation patterns. Across durations of 0.5–10 s, brief stimulation generated measurable stimulus-associated signals, and response magnitude, persistence, and spatial distribution varied with stimulus duration. For paired 2-s stimuli, trial-level separability was already high at the shortest tested 1-s gap, corresponding to a 3-s onset-to-onset spacing, and reached 100% at gaps of 3 s or longer. Building on the experimentally characterized spatiotemporal response properties of fUS-CBV signals, a proof-of-concept modeling and decoding framework was developed, comprising cross-animal spatial prediction, classification of short versus long stimulation from S1BF ΔCBV time courses with known stimulus onset, and modeling of paired-event separability. Together, the results show that fUS-CBV signals retain structured spatial and temporal information about controlled sensory input after neurovascular transformation. These measured response properties characterize the spatiotemporal boundaries within which neural activity can be reliably distinguished using fUS-CBV signals, providing constraints for the development of fUS-based decoding models and the design of stimulation paradigms suitable for reliable fUS decoding.

title: Input resolution and decoder design shape Transformer-based retinal lesion segmentation: a controlled multi-seed study with zero-shot external evaluation
abstract: Abstract Background: Input resolution is usually reported as apreprocessing setting in retinal lesion segmentation, yet downsamplingcompresses small lesion annotations far more than large ones. We asked howresolution, encoder family and decoder design jointly affect segmentation ofmicroaneurysms, haemorrhages, hard exudates and soft exudates, and how much ofan apparent architecture ranking survives testing. Because input size alsochanges token count, positional-embedding interpolation, window configurationand the memory plan, we estimate resolution-conditioned system performance, notan isolated effect of spatial resolution. Methods: Four ImageNet-pretrained Transformer systems (ViT-Small/16,CaiT-XS24, Swin-Tiny, SwinV2-CR-Tiny) were trained on the FGADR Seg-set at 224,384, 512 and 768 pixels with five seeds each, under one frozen image-disjointpartition, schedule and scoring pipeline. A shared-final-decoder control and afixed-budget GroupNorm U-Net reference completed a frozen base of 120 models,evaluated on a held-out FGADR cohort and by zero-shot transfer to IDRiD.Outcomes were pooled pixel-level AUPR and mean average precision overlesion-positive images. Systems were compared under seed-paired \((t)\)-tests and ahierarchical seed-and-image bootstrap with Holm correction, and by equivalencetesting at margins of 0.01, 0.02 and 0.03. Results: Between 224 and 768 pixels macro pooled AUPR rose for all foursystems on FGADR (0.0794--0.1614) and IDRiD (0.1198--0.2150), but notmonotonically: CaiT-XS24 peaked at 512 pixels, a decline absent on FGADR underpositive-image aggregation. Most multiplicity-adjusted evidence lay in the firststep of the range. Pairwise testing separated systems far more readily underevaluation-cohort than seed resampling; externally at 768 pixels the two agreedon none of ten pairs. The hierarchical systems were equivalent internally at512 pixels and above at margins of 0.02 and 0.03, but not 0.01. A shared decoderreversed the ViT-Small/16 versus SwinV2-CR-Tiny ordering in all four conditions(\((p_{\mathrm{Holm}}=0.004)\)), an encoder--decoder interaction. Macro calibrationerror fell in all eight Transformer conditions (sign test \((p=0.008)\)), andtraining cost per epoch rose 11- to 38-fold. Conclusions: The benefit of resolution is neither universal, nordecoder-independent, nor free, and part of it depends on how performance isaggregated over lesion-negative images. Resolution, encoder and decoder shouldbe chosen together and reported with calibration, aggregation and measuredcompute.

title: Effects of a Ciprofol-Etomidate Mixture on Intraoperative Hypoxemia and Hypotension in Older Patients Undergoing Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Under Sedation: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the efficacy and safety of a 1:1 ciprofol-etomidate mixture for sedation during combined gastrointestinal endoscopy in older patients and to provide evidence for optimizing clinical sedation strategies. Methods This single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial enrolled 203 patients aged 60–80 years who were scheduled to undergo combined gastrointestinal endoscopy under sedation. Patients were randomly assigned to receive either ciprofol alone (Group C, n = 101) or a ciprofol-etomidate mixture (Group CE, n = 102). Patients in Group C received intravenous ciprofol at a dose of 0.3 mg/kg, whereas those in Group CE received a slow intravenous injection of a ciprofol-etomidate mixture comprising ciprofol 0.15 mg/kg and etomidate 0.12 mg/kg over 1 min. The primary outcome was the composite incidence of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxemia. Secondary outcomes included adverse events, sedation onset time, first-dose sedation success rate, recovery time, and satisfaction scores reported by patients, anesthesiologists, and endoscopists. Results The incidence of the composite outcome of intraoperative hypotension and hypoxemia was significantly lower in Group CE than in Group C (P < 0.05). Group CE also had significantly lower incidences of hypotension (21.2% vs. 42.3%) and vasopressor use (15.4% vs. 34.6%) (both P = 0.001). Sedation onset was significantly faster in Group CE than in Group C (61.0 ± 6.1 s vs. 71.1 ± 14.4 s), the first-dose sedation success rate was higher (97.1% vs. 89.4%), and recovery time was shorter (18.3 ± 3.8 min vs. 19.6 ± 4.2 min) (all P < 0.05). The incidences of myoclonus and injection pain did not differ significantly between the groups ( P > 0.05). Anesthesiologist satisfaction was significantly higher in Group CE than in Group C (P < 0.001), whereas patient and endoscopist satisfaction scores were comparable between the groups. Conclusion A 1:1 ciprofol-etomidate mixture improves hemodynamic stability, accelerates sedation onset, and increases the first-dose sedation success rate in older patients undergoing gastrointestinal endoscopy under sedation, without increasing adverse events. This regimen may enhance the efficiency of anesthesia management and represents a potentially useful clinical sedation strategy. Trial registration The trial was registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2500103032, https//www.chictr.org.cn/)on 23/05/2025.

title: Automated cross-modal framework enables whole-brain mesoscale connectivity mapping in macaques
abstract: Abstract Advances in whole-brain ex vivo imaging enable large-scale, cellular-resolution mapping of macaque brain architecture and connectivity. However, the seamless integration of multimodal datasets at scale remains challenging due to substantial tissue deformation, cross-modal contrast discrepancies, and individual morphological variability. Here, we present Macaca-Star, a high-throughput, fully automated framework for cross-modal whole-brain mapping in macaques. Macaca-Star synergizes modality-specific preprocessing, deep learning–based cross-modal translation, and optional subject-specific in vivo MRI guidance to achieve robust spatial and modal alignment. This end-to-end system reconciles these disparities, eliminates manual intervention and reduces the processing time from weeks to hours while maintaining high anatomical fidelity. It effectively maps both 3D volumetric and 2D section-based optical data into a unified anatomical space, enabling precise spatial integration of cytoarchitectural features, axonal projections, and neuronal somata. To demonstrate its discovery potential, we applied Macaca-Star to integrate fMOST-derived anterograde tracing with section-based retrograde tracing data. This integration resolved subregional connectivity patterns within the temporoparietal and insular areas that were previously difficult to unify across disparate imaging scales. Overall, Macaca-Star offers a versatile platform for multimodal data fusion, advancing comprehensive connectivity and atlas-based analysis in the primate brain.

title: Development of a Deep Learning Model Integrating Computed Tomography Images and Blood Data for the Diagnosis of Acute Cholecystitis
abstract: Abstract Background In this study, we aimed to develop and evaluate an artificial intelligence-based diagnostic model for the diagnosis of acute cholecystitis (AC) using non-contrast CT images and clinical data. Methods This retrospective study included 197 patients (100 AC, 97 non-AC) treated between January 2016 and December 2025 at a single center. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 139) and test (n = 58) datasets. Three models were constructed: an imaging-based deep learning model, a clinical data-based machine learning model, and a hybrid machine learning model integrating deep learning-derived imaging features with clinical data. CT images were preprocessed, and gallbladder regions were segmented. Clinical variables included white blood cell counts and levels of C-reactive protein and liver function markers. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, specificity, F1 score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Statistical comparisons were performed using Welch's t-test and Chi-square test. Results The imaging-based model achieved accuracy 0.741, precision 0.703, recall 0.867, specificity 0.607, F1 score 0.776, and AUC 0.863. The blood-based model achieved accuracy 0.914, precision 0.931, recall 0.900, specificity 0.929, F1 score 0.915, and AUC 0.946. The hybrid model showed the highest performance, with accuracy 0.931, precision 0.882, recall 1.000, specificity 0.857, F1 score 0.938, and AUC 0.996. Conclusions A hybrid model integrating CT imaging and clinical data improved diagnostic performance for AC compared with single-modality models.

The blood-based model achieved accuracy 0.914, precision 0.931, recall 0.900, specificity 0.929, F1 score 0.915, and AUC 0.946. The hybrid model showed the highest performance, with accuracy 0.931, precision 0.882, recall 1.000, specificity 0.857, F1 score 0.938, and AUC 0.996. Conclusions A hybrid model integrating CT imaging and clinical data improved diagnostic performance for AC compared with single-modality models.

title: An Interpretable Multimodal Machine Learning Model for Predicting Early Hematoma Progression in Bifrontal Cerebral Contusion
abstract: Abstract Objective To develop and validate a risk prediction model for early hematoma progression (HP) in patients with bifrontal cerebral contusions, systematically compare the performance of multiple machine learning algorithms, identify an optimal model with robustness, generalizability, and clinical interpretability, and determine the key factors driving HP. Methods This dual-center retrospective study included 1,100 adult patients with radiologically confirmed bifrontal cerebral contusions. The modeling cohort comprised 454 patients from the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University and was randomly divided into a training set of 318 patients and an internal validation set of 136 patients. An independent cohort of 646 patients from the Second Affiliated Hospital of the University of South China was used for external validation. Demographic characteristics, vital signs, laboratory indicators, and cranial computed tomography features were collected, with HP defined as the outcome. To minimize information leakage, preprocessing, feature selection, model fitting, and hyperparameter optimization were conducted exclusively within the training set. A two-stage feature-selection strategy combining random forest importance ranking and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used to identify the core predictors, which were subsequently applied unchanged to the internal and external validation cohorts. Thirteen machine learning models were developed, and their discrimination, classification performance, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated. Shapley Additive Explanations were used to characterize global and patient-level contributions of the predictors to the selected model. Results The intersection of features selected by RF and Lasso yielded 10 stable core predictors: time to baseline CT, ventricular compression, sulcal effacement, hematoma density coefficient of variation (Hematoma.DCV), heart rate, white blood cell count, eosinophil count, albumin, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI). Among the 13 models, LightGBM achieved the highest apparent training-set AUC of 0.872 but decreased to 0.652 in the internal validation set, a pattern consistent with limited generalizability and possible overfitting. In contrast, Lasso achieved the numerically highest AUC in the internal validation set, with an AUC of 0.764 (95% CI: 0.677–0.852). In the external cohort, its AUC decreased to 0.694 but remained numerically higher than those of the other models displayed in the external ROC analysis. Because formal pairwise statistical comparisons were not available, these findings should not be interpreted as demonstrating the statistical superiority of Lasso over the other models. External decision curve analysis indicated potential net benefit mainly at low threshold probabilities, whereas calibration was suboptimal (Hosmer–Lemeshow χ²=33.87, P < 0.001; Brier score = 0.2405), with a tendency to underestimate observed HP risk. SHAP analysis indicated that Hematoma.DCV, time to baseline CT, MLR, sulcal effacement, PNI, heart rate, and ventricular compression were the main drivers of model prediction. Conclusion In patients with bifrontal cerebral contusions, the Lasso model showed comparatively stable discrimination and greater structural interpretability than the higher-capacity ensemble models. However, external discrimination was modest, calibration was inadequate, and clinical net benefit was mainly confined to low threshold probabilities. Hematoma density heterogeneity, the timing of baseline CT, systemic inflammatory–immune–nutritional status, and local intracranial compression signs contributed importantly to model predictions. The model should currently be regarded as a supplementary risk-ranking approach rather than a stand-alone screening tool or a source of directly actionable absolute-risk estimates. External recalibration and larger multicenter prospective validation are required before clinical implementation.

title: CBCT-based three-dimensional morphometric analysis of the upper airway and its influencing factors in skeletal Class II average-angle patients across different bone ages
abstract: Abstract Objective Previous studies have largely treated skeletal Class II patients as a homogeneous group for overall analysis, without fully accounting for subgroup differences in vertical facial patterns or variations in developmental timing. Consequently, a systematic understanding of the associations between upper airway morphology, hyoid position, and craniofacial morphology remains insufficient, which limits the formulation of precise clinical intervention strategies. This study aims to analyze the three-dimensional morphological changes of the upper airway and their associated influencing factors in skeletal Class II average-angle patients, stratified by cervical vertebral bone age staging, so as to provide evidence for the development of stage-specific orthodontic treatment strategies. Methods A total of 205 skeletal Class II average-angle patients were enrolled and divided into four groups (T1–T4) according to cervical vertebral bone age staging. Upper airway morphology, hyoid position, and craniofacialparameters were assessed using cone-beam CT (CBCT) three-dimensional reconstruction combined with Dolphin and WinCeph software. Inter-group comparisons were conducted using analysis of variance (ANOVA). Spearman correlation analysis and multiple linear regression analysis were used to identify independent predictors of upper airway morphology. Results In females, total upper airway volume and nasopharyngeal volume increased significantly at stages T2 and T4, whereas palatopharyngeal and laryngopharyngeal volumes showed significant increased only at stage T4 ( P < 0.05). In males, significant volumetric increments across all airway segments were observed predominantly at stages T3 and T4 ( P < 0.05). Multiple regression analysis revealed that in females, the positive predictors of total upper airway volume included bone age stages T2 and T4, Mx'-Mx, H-RGn, and H-CVP. In males, the positive predictors comprised bone age stage T3, H-RGn, and H-CVP. Conclusion Upper airway volume in skeletal Class II average-angle patients exhibits a sex-dimorphic developmental pattern across bone age stages. Females display a biphasic growth pattern with leap-like increases at T2 and T4, whereas males demonstrate a steady and pronounced growth spurt from T3 to T4. Hyoid position parameters (H-RGn and H-CVP) consistently emerge as key determinants of upper airway volume, while the contribution of jaw morphology—primarily maxillary width—varies by gender.

title: A predictive model for adjuvant chemotherapy benefit in locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma integrating post-treatment multi-sequence MRI radiomics and dynamic clinical biomarkers: a retrospective single-center cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background The benefit of adjuvant chemotherapy (AC) for locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC) is uncertain. We aimed to develop a model integrating post-treatment MRI radiomics and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) DNA to identify patients who benefit from AC. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 267 patients with LA-NPC treated at a single institution. A radiomic-clinical signature (RCS) for predicting 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) was constructed using radiomic features extracted from post-concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) multi-sequence MRI and dynamic EBV DNA data. Model performance was evaluated using Harrell's concordance index (C-index). Patients were stratified into high- and low-risk subgroups based on the RCS, and the survival benefit of AC was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis. Results The cohort was randomly divided into training (n = 213) and testing (n = 54) sets. The fused RCS model achieved C-indices of 0.899 and 0.719 for predicting 2-year PFS in the training and testing sets, respectively, outperforming models using clinical (0.583) or radiomic (0.695) features alone. Risk stratification by the RCS identified low- and high-risk groups with significantly different survival outcomes (all p < 0.05). Subgroup analysis showed that AC significantly improved 2-year PFS only in the high-risk group (94.3% vs. 87.0%, p = 0.045), with no benefit observed in low-risk patients. Conclusions The RCS model effectively stratifies patients with LA-NPC and may guide personalized AC decisions by identifying high-risk patients likely to benefit. Trial registration Not applicable. This was a retrospective observational study and was not registered as a clinical trial.

title: A Pixel-based Confidence Weighted Transfusion model for Colonoscopy and Colon Capsule Endoscopy image-based Polyp Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Polyps one of the most frequently occurring lesions in the human gastrointestinal system and play a critical role in colorectal cancer development, often serving as early indicators or precursors of malignant transformation. Timely and early detection of polyps is critical for lowering the risk of colorectal cancer and increasing survival. Polyp segmentation is crucial in improving computer-aided detection and diagnosis systems, which may support early intervention. CNN-based segmentation models often struggle to capture global contextual information, leading to suboptimal performance. These limitations are further amplified in endoscopic imaging scenarios, where variable resolution in colon capsule endoscopies (CCE) and conventional colonoscopy images—introduces inconsistencies in feature representation and contextual awareness. Therefore, we develop a comprehensive TransFuseNet model that captures local and global receptive fields at the encoder and decoder levels. The pixel-based confidence-weighted fusion combines features from two models, which facilitates knowledge and domain shift features that allows segmentation of low- and high-resolution images. We validated the model's performance on seven diverse optical colonoscopies, CCE, and synthetic datasets. Analysis reveals that our developed model has yielded an intersection over the union of 84.67\%, 89.05\%, 88.91\%, 89.46\%, 89.58\%, 82.07\%, and 86.41\% on the Kvasir, CVC-300, CVC-ColonDB, CVC-ClinicDB, ETIS, CCE CareForColon2015 dataset, and Synthetic datasets, respectively. The external validation also confirms the robustness and effectiveness of our developed model, providing a new pathway for polyp segmentation using optical colonoscopy and CCE images with explainable characteristics and polyp pixel measurement. Thus, our proposed TransFuseNet effectively handles both low- and high-resolution endoscopic images by fusing local and global contextual features. This supports more reliable polyp segmentation across diverse imaging conditions, enhancing diagnostic accuracy in clinical practice.

title: Analysis of Influencing Factors and Development of a Clinical Prediction Model for Postoperative Visual Improvement Prognosis in Patients with Age-Related Cataract
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To identify independent factors associated with postoperative visual improvement after phacoemulsification combined with intraocular lens (IOL) implantation in patients with age-related cataract (ARC) and to develop an interpretable individualized clinical prediction nomogram for preoperative risk stratification. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included 1,847 eyes with ARC who underwent phacoemulsification combined with IOL implantation. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors associated with postoperative visual improvement. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling with 1,000 iterations. Model performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, calibration curve, decision curve analysis (DCA), and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) value analysis. Results: Age, severity of preoperative visual impairment, fundus lesions, axial length, and keratometric value (K-value) were identified as independent predictors of postoperative visual improvement. The prediction model demonstrated good discriminative ability, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.83 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78–0.89) in the training cohort and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.70–0.86) in the validation cohort. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed outcomes, and decision curve analysis indicated favorable clinical utility. SHAP analysis revealed that age contributed most significantly to the model prediction. A visual nomogram was subsequently developed to provide individualized risk estimation. Conclusion: The nomogram incorporating five independent predictors demonstrated good discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability for predicting postoperative visual improvement in patients with ARC. This model may serve as a practical tool for preoperative risk assessment, individualized patient counseling, and doctor–patient communication.

title: Augmented Surgical Fixation of Pelvic Fractures in Elderly Patients. A prospective case series study from level one trauma centre in Upper Egypt
abstract: Abstract Purpose The purpose of this study was to evaluate functional outcomes after augmenting surgical fixation of pelvic fractures in elderly patients and to identify clinical and surgical factors influencing recovery, particularly the role of early mobilization. Methods This prospective case series was conducted at Assiut University Trauma Hospital, which is level 1 trauma center, between May 2023 and July 2024. This study included 15 patients aged ≥ 65 years with pelvic fractures treated surgically using minimally invasive augmented surgical fixation techniques. Preoperative evaluation included clinical assessment, pelvic radiographs, and CT scans, with fractures classified according to the Rommens classification and AO/OTA systems. Posterior stabilization was performed using transsacral screws, with additional anterior fixation using INFIX or locked symphyseal plating when indicated. The primary outcome was post surgery weightbearing pain assessed by the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), while secondary outcomes included functional evaluation using the Majeed's score and Merle d’Aubigné score, radiological union and implant loosening. Follow-up was performed up to one year. Results Fifteen patients were included (mean age 67.7 ± 3.2 years), with a predominance of males (86.7%). Most injuries resulted from low-energy trauma (60%). According to Rommens classifications, types II–III fractures were most common fractures to be included, while AO/OTA type B fractures predominated. Transsacral screw fixation was the most frequently used technique (60%), often combined with anterior stabilization methods. Median intraoperative blood loss was 30 ml and mean radiation exposure was 2.76 ± 0.87 mSv. Significant improvement was observed in clinical outcomes during follow-up, with VAS scores decreasing from 3.47 ± 1.25 at 3 weeks to 0.85 ± 0.90 at 1 year (p < 0.001) and Majeed scores improving from 58 ± 12 at 1.5 months to 89 ± 10 at 1 year (p < 0.001). Delayed weight bearing and higher early pain scores were strongly associated with poorer functional outcomes. Early postoperative pain was the only independent predictor of the 1-year Majeed score. One-year mortality was 13.3%, radiological union occurred in 92.3% of patients, and implant loosening occurred in 23% without requiring reoperation. Conclusion Augmented fixation techniques provide stable management of pelvic fractures in elderly patients, facilitating early mobilization and significant functional improvement. Early pain control and timely weight bearing appear to be key determinants of recovery.

title: Complex Müllerian Duct Anomaly Presenting as a Rare OHVIRA Variant: Clinical and Surgical Perspectives
abstract: Abstract Background Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Agenesis (OHVIRA) syndrome, also referred to as Herlyn–Werner–Wunderlich syndrome, is an uncommon congenital anomaly of the genitourinary tract characterized by uterine malformations, an obstructed hemivagina, and ipsilateral renal agenesis. Atypical variants add further complexity, often posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 14-year-old girl presenting with primary amenorrhea and cyclical abdominal pain. Imaging revealed a bicornuate unicollis uterus with hematometrocolpos, absent left kidney, and a grossly dilated ectopic right ureter. Intraoperatively, the cervix was rudimentary and hypoplastic, precluding fertility preservation. A complete hysterectomy with right ureteric reimplantation was performed using the Politano–Leadbetter technique. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the patient experienced complete resolution of symptoms at follow-up. Discussion This case demonstrates an atypical variant of Obstructed Hemivagina and Ipsilateral Renal Agenesis (OHVIRA) syndrome, characterized by bicornuate uterus, rudimentary cervix, segmental vaginal atresia, unilateral renal agenesis, and ureteric malpositioning. Such complex anomalies underscore the limitations of current classification systems and emphasize the importance of detailed anatomical description. Magnetic resonance imaging remains the diagnostic gold standard, while multidisciplinary planning is crucial for tailoring management to individual patients. When reconstructive options are not feasible, definitive surgical intervention is often required to achieve symptom relief and prevent long-term morbidity. Conclusion Atypical variants of OHVIRA syndrome underscore the importance of integrating embryological understanding, systematic renal screening, and collaborative surgical planning. Early recognition and tailored intervention are critical to achieving symptom relief and preventing long-term morbidity.

title: Evaluating Boundary-Aware Losses for U-KAN on BraTS 2023 Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Background:: Boundary-aware loss functions are intended to improve segmentation by penalizing spatial errors that may be insufficiently represented by region-based objectives. Whether they provide meaningful and reproducible benefits when incorporated into U-KAN for brain tumor segmentation remains unclear. Methods: : We compared five loss configurations in separate 2D and 3D U-KAN pipelines using multimodal MRI from the BraTS 2023 adult glioma dataset: a region-based baseline, fixed Boundary Loss, Staged Boundary Loss, a Generalized Surface Loss composite, and standalone Boundary Difference-over-Union loss. Each configuration was trained with three seeds in each pipeline, producing 30 runs. Performance was assessed using regional and macro Dice, the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), run-level consistency, and patient-level paired comparisons against the corresponding baseline. Results: : In 2D, Staged Boundary Loss achieved the highest mean macro Dice (0.8139 versus 0.8001) and reduced mean HD95 (22.55 versus 34.81~mm). Patient-level comparisons favored this configuration, but its overlap improvement was concentrated in whole-tumor segmentation and it exceeded the baseline in only one of three matched seed comparisons. In 3D, Staged Boundary Loss produced only small descriptive improvements in macro Dice (0.89794 versus 0.89698) and HD95 (3.645 versus 3.736~mm), with no significant favorable patient-level difference after multiplicity correction. title: Benign Struma Ovarii Presenting as a Large Multicytic Ovarian Mass: Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Struma ovarii is a very rare form of ovarian teratoma with thyroid tissue present in the ovarian mass. A struma ovarii is categorised based on 50% or more of solid tissue being thyroid tissues. This particular entity can be an adult teratoma with distinct diagnostic challenges by virtue of its peculiar features, including thyroid hormone production. The tentative diagnosis is examined in a perimenopausal woman, with long-standing lower abdominal distention. Case Presentation: A 42-year-old woman, with a parity of 4 presented with a two-year history of intermittent episodes of dull lower abdominal pain associated with a feeling of a mass descending across her abdomen. This was associated with episodes of nausea, occasional vomiting, and dyspareunia for about five months. The patient also had irregular heavy menstrual periods for a similar duration. History did not reveal any signs of hyperthyroidism, Abnormal Uterine bleeding nor urinary tract symptoms. On physical examination, a firm, immobile, well-defined suprapubic mass was noted. Evaluation with abdominopelvic ultrasound showed a large, complex left adnexal cystic lesion with multiple septations. The patient was taken up for an exploratory laparotomy. Intraoperatively, a large, tortuous, multi cystic mass and highly vascularized, arising from the left ovary was found, and a left salpingo-oophorectomy was performed. Histopathological examination revealed a multicystic ovary with solid areas that contained seromucinous fluid and hemorrhage. Histological verification was made by the demonstration of ovarian tissue containing 80–90% benign thyroid follicles of varied sizes lined with cuboidal epithelium; with foci of calcification; and no evidence of malignancy. The patient made an uneventful postoperative recovery Conclusion Struma ovarii is tough to diagnose because it mimics so many other conditions and rarely causes thyroid symptoms. In women of reproductive age who have complex ovarian masses, it’s worth keeping in mind, even if their thyroid tests are normal. The only way to be sure is to look at the tissue under a microscope after surgery, which, for benign cases, also solves the problem.

title: Pretreatment Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio as a Risk Marker for Brain Metastasis in Patients with Stage I–III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Receiving Definitive Thoracic Radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Background Brain metastasis (BM) represents a major pattern of distant failure in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following definitive thoracic radiotherapy (RT). Systemic inflammation plays a critical role in tumor progression and the metastatic cascade. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of the baseline neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) for predicting the occurrence, cumulative incidence, and temporal dynamics of brain metastasis in patients with Stage I–III NSCLC receiving definitive thoracic RT. Methods A total of 138 patients with pathologically confirmed Stage I–III NSCLC who received definitive-intent thoracic RT (60–66 Gy) between 2014 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Pre-treatment hematological parameters were obtained within two weeks prior to any oncological intervention. Time-dependent Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated the dynamic predictive performance of baseline NLR. Independent predictors of brain failure were identified using cause-specific Cox proportional hazards regression, accounting for death as a competing risk. A pre-specified sensitivity analysis was restricted to Stage III patients (n = 108) with mandatory baseline and routine follow-up brain MRI. Results Over a median follow-up of 28.0 months, 40 patients (29.0%) developed BM. Median baseline NLR was significantly higher in patients who developed BM compared to those who did not (3.21 vs. 2.22; p < 0.001). Time-dependent ROC analysis at 28 months yielded an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.79, with an optimal NLR threshold of 2.26 (sensitivity: 91.7%, specificity: 54.6%). Multivariable cause-specific Cox regression demonstrated that higher continuous baseline NLR was independently associated with an increased hazard of BM (HR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.48–2.12; p < 0.001), alongside adenocarcinoma histology (HR: 2.96, 95% CI: 1.41–6.24; p = 0.004). In the Stage III sub-cohort sensitivity analysis, continuous baseline NLR maintained its independent prognostic significance (HR: 1.74, 95% CI: 1.44–2.09; p < 0.001). High baseline NLR (> 2.26) was significantly associated with a higher cumulative incidence of BM (Gray’s test p < 0.001), inferior overall survival (median 34.0 vs. 65.0 months; p = 0.015), and worse progression-free survival (median 18.0 vs. 42.0 months; p = 0.006). Baseline PLR was not significantly associated with BM (p = 0.136). Conclusions Continuous baseline NLR serves as a readily accessible, independent biomarker for predicting the risk and accelerated onset of brain metastasis in patients with NSCLC undergoing definitive chemoradiotherapy. Baseline NLR may aid in risk-stratified neuro-radiological surveillance protocols.

title: Airway Fire During Left Pneumonectomy: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background. Intraoperative airway fire is extremely rare yet potentially fatal, and an oxygen-filled tracheal tube is a major risk factor. Fire during pneumonectomy—in which the airway is simultaneously the operative field, the sole ventilatory route, and the conduit for combustion—is uniquely hazardous. We describe such a case and analyze its mechanism, management, and prevention. Case presentation. A 70-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and a long history of smoking underwent thoracoscopic resection of a centrally located left-lower-lobe squamous cell carcinoma. During left pneumonectomy, while the left main bronchus was being divided with monopolar electrosurgery, sudden flame and smoke indicated combustion of the double-lumen tube, which was judged nonventilatable and urgently changed to a single-lumen tube. Before chest closure, bronchoscopy showed red, edematous mucosa with diffuse black carbonized deposits over the carina and both main bronchi; four intraoperative lavage passes were performed, and three further passes were carried out intermittently while the patient remained intubated in the intensive care unit. He was extubated on the first postoperative day, developed transient atrial fibrillation on the second, and was discharged on the seventh. Histopathology confirmed keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma (pT4N2M0, stage IIIB). Conclusions. Recognition of the fuel–oxidizer–ignition triad, and preventive measures adopted before and during bronchial division, are essential. Once a fire occurs, immediate cessation of oxygen, rapid re-establishment of a ventilatable airway, aggressive bronchoscopic saline lavage, glucocorticoid pulse therapy, and supportive postoperative care together supported a favorable outcome; at follow-up the patient had completed five cycles of chemotherapy, with intermittent cough and sputum production and hoarseness attributed to unilateral vocal cord paralysis, but remained able to carry out the activities of daily living without clinically significant laryngotracheal stenosis.

title: Anatomical Interfaces as a Complementary Substrate for Structural MRI Representation in Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: Abstract Background Structural MRI analysis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) commonly relies on region-of-interest (ROI) summaries or voxel-level deep networks, neither of which explicitly quantifies the physical interfaces shared by adjacent brain regions. We investigated whether these anatomical interfaces provide structural information complementary to conventional regional measures. Methods T1-weighted MRI was segmented into 79 anatomical regions using a pretrained nnU-Net. Each region was represented as a graph node with six morpho-textural descriptors, while edges were defined only between regions sharing voxel-level face contact and characterized by Structural Contact and Boundary Appearance features. Results Correlation analyses showed generally limited redundancy between node- and interface-level descriptors, supporting partially distinct representational information. Node-controlled analyses further showed that selected interface features remained significantly associated with disease stage after adjustment for the morpho-textural characteristics of both connected regions, indicating that interface-level variation was not fully reducible to regional abnormalities. White matter hypointensity interfaces repeatedly emerged among the retained stage-associated effects. Selected Structural Contact features also showed convergent associations with clinical severity across CDR-SB, ADAS-Cog13, and MMSE. Representation ablation demonstrated that disrupting anatomical adjacency or removing interface attributes reduced classification performance, supporting the contribution of anatomically organized relational information. The full representation also improved multi-class classification relative to conventional ROI-vector and voxel-level baselines, with this advantage preserved on the independent NACC cohort without fine-tuning. Conclusions These findings indicate that anatomical interfaces provide measurable and complementary structural information beyond conventional region-wise morphometry, offering an interpretable framework for representing inter-regional structural relationships in neurodegenerative disease.

title: Association of TREM1 rs2234246 with miR-138-5p-dependent reporter regulation, TREM1 expression, and hippocampal volume in Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder in which neuroinflammation contributes to disease pathogenesis. Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 1 (TREM1) has been implicated in inflammatory responses, and the functional polymorphism rs2234246, located in the 3′-untranslated region (UTR) of TREM1, has been associated with TREM1 expression and brain amyloid deposition. We hypothesized that rs2234246 regulates TREM1 expression through microRNA (miR)-138-5p and is associated with AD-related neurodegenerative changes. To test this hypothesis, we performed SNP functional analysis, dual-luciferase reporter assays, peripheral blood expression analyses o f membrane form ( mbTREM1 ), soluble form ( TREM1sv ), and miR-138-5p, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based hippocampal volumetric analyses. The rs2234246 A allele was associated with increased mbTREM1 mRNA expression but not TREM1sv expression. Dual-luciferase reporter assays demonstrated allele-dependent reporter repression consistent with an interaction between miR-138-5p and the TREM1 3′-UTR containing the A allele. In patients with AD, plasma TREM-1 protein concentration and miR-138-5p expression were significantly increased, whereas TREM1sv expression was significantly decreased. Furthermore, the rs2234246 A allele was associated with reduced right hippocampal volume in patients with AD. These findings provide complementary evidence of allele-dependent reporter regulation involving miR-138-5p, altered peripheral TREM1-related expression in AD, and an exploratory association between rs2234246 and right hippocampal volume. Further studies are required to clarify the biological relationships among these findings and their relevance to AD pathogenesis.

title: Artificial intelligence for equitable precision in head and neck cancer care
abstract: Abstract Dear Editor,l appreciate Karunya et al.'s comprehensive review of the epidemiology, global burden, and evolution of head and neck cancer radiotherapy (HNC)[1], and believe that artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to link all of these technological advances to earlier diagnosis, more personalised treatment and more equitable access to radiotherapy. First, AI can solve some real world challenges of high quality radiotherapy planning. The use of deep-learning systems for automatic segmentation of target volumes and organs at risk (OAR), the prediction of achievable dose distributions, supporting plan optimization, and quality assurance (QA) is of particular relevance in HNC, where target volumes are often irregularly shaped and closely contiguous to the salivary glands, pharyngeal constrictors, spinal cord, brainstem, and other radiosensitive organs. In some studies, AI-driven planning has shown to save time and improve the quality of plans, while in others, it has been found to be as efficient as traditional planning, but further clinical validation is required[2]. The potential impact of AI on ART could be even more pronounced during this multiple-week course of radiotherapy, as changes in the position of the tumour, weight loss, and tumour regression can affect target coverage or the dose to normal tissue. Cone beam computed tomography enhancement or generation, automatic re-contouring, dose recalculation and identification of patients likely to benefit from replanning are all aspects of the ART pathway that can be accelerated with the help of AI. There is promising performance for AI-based OAR segmentation, models to predict the need for adaptation, and it was noted that the evidence available to date is largely retrospective, and so human review should be integral, especially for tumour boundaries and small critical structures[3]. Last, the advantages of AI-assisted ART should be measured by clinically meaningful outcomes, not just geometric precision, such as xerostomia, dysphagia, and dependence on feeding tubes, among other toxicities. Second, AI can help to enhance early detection and risk-based referral in areas with high burden. Smartphone assisted oral examination is a potentially scalable option for delayed presentation in India, where tobacco use, areca-nut consumption, alcohol consumption and lack of specialists are involved in delayed presentation. Such models could be applied to aid prioritization of oral potentially malignant disorder cases for teleconsultation or biopsy or specialist referral in Indian community screening datasets, using deep-learning algorithms applied to oral photographs acquired by trained frontline health workers[4] They need to be used as a triage tool, however, not as a stand-alone diagnostic instrument. The performance of any algorithm must be assessed in a variety of populations, devices, lighting conditions, lesion locations, and levels of health worker training and training, or otherwise, the algorithm may actually exacerbate diagnostic disparities and inequities. Limited external validation, methodological inconsistencies, and a lack of prospective studies are also identified as significant challenges in the broader HNC AI literature[5].Third, AI offers a chance to shift away from anatomy-based treatment decision. Models that take into account HPV or p16 status, smoking history, tumour subsite, imaging, digital pathology, molecular markers and longitudinal treatment data could be used to estimate locoregional control, distant failure, survival and toxicity for each individual patient. These estimates could ultimately help inform treatment-intensity decisions, biomarker-directed treatment selection criteria, surveillance planning, and biomarker-directed trial eligibility[6]. Therefore, although evidence suggests that radiomic models have moderate diagnostic accuracy, at this time, there is not enough consistent evidence to replace the currently validated pathological HPV testing and treatment de-intensification should be reserved for appropriately designed clinical trials. More generally, models using clinical and radiomic data have yielded promising results for predicting tumour control and radiotherapy toxicity, but need larger, multi-institutional datasets and prospective validation[7]. A pathway to implementation that would be constructive would be the four following steps that would be pre-clinical “silent mode” evaluation of the software prior to use; software validation across institutions, imaging vendors, treatment platforms, and subgroups; deployment of the software with uncertainty alert systems and auditable overrides; and post-implementation monitoring for software toxicity, disease control, workflow efficiency, and subgroups performance. Resource limited centres should not be recipients of models developed in only a well-resourced centre, but should also be a co-design and validation centre. It will be critical that the software is lightweight, that it integrates easily with current CT and linear-accelerator equipment, that calibration can be completed locally, that the workforce can be trained to use it, and that its cost-effectiveness is easily understood. Federated or distributed learning can also enable collaborative model improvements, without the need to centralize sensitive patient information. The review by Karunya et al. serves as a useful framework in which to consider how responsibly validated AI may help enhance planning accuracy, the ability for adaptive treatment, improving early detection and biologically driven personalization. But “automation for the sake of automation” isn't the priority; the goal should be to deliver measurable and equitable improvements in patient outcomes.

title: Preoperative Risk Stratification of Lymph Node Metastasis in cT1 Lung Adenocarcinoma Using CT Radiomics and Habitat Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate preoperative assessment of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is important for risk stratification and surgical planning in patients with cT1 lung adenocarcinoma. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a multi-regional computed tomography (CT) radiomics model incorporating intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat information for preoperative prediction of LNM. Methods A total of 172 patients with cT1 invasive lung adenocarcinoma from one institution were retrospectively included and randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 120) and an internal validation cohort (n = 52). An independent cohort of 63 patients from a second institution was used for external validation. Radiomic features were extracted from the intratumoral region, a 3-mm peritumoral region, and two habitat subregions generated using K-means clustering. After feature selection, a multi-regional radiomic signature (Radscore) was constructed and combined with preoperative clinical variables using logistic regression. title: Hierarchical transfer learning and region of interest standardization for bone age assessment in Thai children
abstract: Abstract \normalfont\unboldmath Bone age assessment (BAA) from hand radiographs is routinely used to evaluate child growth and endocrine disorders, but manual atlas-based reading is slow and reader-dependent, while deep learning models trained on large international datasets may lose accuracy in other populations. We developed a population-specific AI framework for BAA in Thai children. It combines ROI standardization using contrast enhancement, automatic hand detection, and segmentation with an EfficientNetB7 regression model trained through hierarchical transfer learning. The model first learned skeletal-maturity representations from the public RSNA and DHA datasets and was then fine-tuned on Thai hospital data. On a held-out Thai test set excluded from BAA training and validation, hierarchical adaptation achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.64 months (RMSE, 5.85 months; \((R^2=0.98)\)), compared with 5.73 months for pooled training and 7.60 months for the public-only baseline. The full preprocessing pipeline also reduced downstream MAE relative to raw radiographs. It met the predefined detection-and-segmentation processing criterion for all evaluated RSNA and DHA images; however, this finding represents processing completeness rather than independent quantitative validation of segmentation accuracy. Among GP, TW, and a hybrid strategy using TW when applicable and GP outside the validated TW3-RUS range, the hybrid produced the lowest point-estimate MAE, although its advantage over TW was small. Grad-CAM provided exploratory evidence of attention to anatomically relevant regions but also identified localized or non-skeletal attention. Improved RSNA hand ROI annotations are released to support future research.
