title: Prediction of Lymphovascular Invasion in Breast Cancer Using Intratumoral and Peritumoral MRI Radiomics Models Based on DCE-MRI: A Multicenter Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose This study explores the predictive value of intramural and peritumoral radiomics features based on dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) for lymphovascular invasion (LVI) in breast cancer. It compares the predictive efficacy of different peritumoral regions and feature fusion methods, and constructs a combined prediction model integrating clinical characteristics. Materials and Methods Retrospectively collected images from 757 breast cancer patients with pathologically confirmed diagnoses who underwent breast DCE-MRI examinations at two medical centers. Data from Center 1 served as the training set (n = 529), while data from Center 2 formed the external validation set (n = 228). Tumor lesions were semi-automatically delineated using ITK-SNAP software, with peritumoral regions automatically expanded. Regions of interest (ROIs) were selected on the maximum intensity phase of DCE-MRI. Radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics across four modalities: intratumoral, peritumoral (1mm, 3mm, 5mm, 7mm, 10mm, 15mm, 20mm), Tumor+Peri7mm, and ImageFusion7 (a fusion of tumor and optimal 7mm peritumoral regions). Data dimensionality reduction and feature selection were performed using Spearman correlation analysis, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, and Maximum Relevance-Minimum Redundancy (mRMR) methods. Five classifiers—support vector machine (SVM), extreme trees (ET), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and multilayer perceptron (MLP)—were evaluated under different feature models to identify the optimal classifier for constructing the radiomics model. Clinical Features: Single- and multi-factor logistic regression screened clinical risk factors to construct a clinical model. Comprehensive evaluations were conducted on the clinical model, the optimal radiomic model, and a combined model incorporating clinical features with optimal radiomic features. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves analyzed predictive performance, with area under the curve (AUC) calculated. A fusion model was established by integrating the radiomic score (rad-score) from the highest-performing predictive model and visualized via a nomogram. The clinical utility of the predictive models was assessed using calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results Clinical characteristics: The AUC values of the clinical model based on histological grade, sentinel lymph node status, and TIC were 0.738 (95% CI: 0.6949–0.7802) and 0.749 (95% CI: 0.6830–0.8141) in the training and validation sets, respectively. As a key indicator reflecting lymph node metastasis in primary tumors, sentinel lymph node status is widely recognized for its role in breast cancer staging and prognostic assessment. For instance, in breast cancer, the area under the ROC curve for a non-sentinel lymph node metastasis risk prediction model in sentinel lymph node-positive patients reached 0.7613, demonstrating its clinical utility. Radiomics: Among the various peritumoral models, the 7 mm peritumoral model demonstrated the best performance. Results indicate that the radiomics model based on the ImageFusion7 (intra-tumor and peritumoral image fusion region) demonstrated optimal diagnostic performance, with the XGBoost classifier showing particularly outstanding results: an AUC of 0.861 (95% CI: 0.8302–0.8914) in the training set and an AUC of 0.709 (95% CI: 0.6407–0.7768). When constructing a clinical-imaging fusion model, the ROC curve based on clinical features and Radscore values achieved AUC values of 0.892 (95% CI: 0.8629–0.9165) and 0.778 (95% CI: 0.7140–0.8375) in the training and validation sets, respectively, surpassing all single models and the intra-tumoral/peritumoral model. The DCA curve demonstrated that the combined model exhibited the highest clinical efficacy and closely followed the diagonal line in the calibration curve, indicating superior model fit and generalization capability. Conclusions An image-based model utilizing DCE-MRI effectively predicts lymphovascular invasion (LVI) status in breast cancer, with the ImageFusion7 model—which integrates images from both the tumor interior and a 7mm peritumoral region—demonstrating optimal predictive performance. Combining this model with clinically independent risk factors further enhances its accuracy. The constructed fusion model exhibits strong discriminatory power and clinical applicability, providing a valuable tool for non-invasive preoperative assessment of LVI risk.

title: Prediction of ERCC1 Expression Level in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Based on Multi-sequence MRI Radiomics and Habitat Analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective To explore the value of multi-sequence MRI-derived radiomics and habitat analysis for predicting excision repair cross-complementation group 1 (ERCC1) expression in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Methods In this retrospective study, 171 patients with non-keratinizing undifferentiated NPC without distant metastasis were enrolled. Patients were stratified into high-ERCC1 (n = 75) and low-ERCC1 (n = 96) groups and randomly split into training (n = 136) and test (n = 35) sets at an 8:2 ratio. Radiomic and habitat features were extracted from T1WI, CE-T1WI and T2WI to calculate radscore and habitat radscore. We constructed radiomics, habitat, clinical, radiomics-clinical and habitat-clinical combined models. Results A total of 14 radiomic features and 20 habitat features were finally selected. Clinical stage (OR = 1.828, 95%CI: 1.011–3.305, P = 0.046) was identified as an independent predictor of high ERCC1 expression. Based on this predictor, five models were constructed: radiomics model, habitat model, radiomics-clinical model, habitat-clinical model and clinical model. Their area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values in the training set were 0.825, 0.917, 0.830, 0.922 and 0.605, respectively; the corresponding AUC values in the test set were 0.770, 0.787, 0.770, 0.807 and 0.537. All radiomics-based models yielded higher AUC values than the clinical model (De Long test, all P < 0.05). The habitat model outperformed the conventional radiomics model in the training set (De Long test, P < 0.05)). Conclusions The Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics and habitat analysis enable effective prediction of ERCC1 expression in NPC patients. The habitat-clinical model achieved the best predictive performance and may support clinical decision-making and prognostic evaluation. The habitat model was superior to conventional radiomics models, suggesting that refined sub-regional segmentation can help boost radiomics prediction accuracy.

title: Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma misdiagnosed as pulmonary embolism: MDM2 amplification as the diagnostic anchor in an unresectable tumor—a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Pulmonary artery intimal sarcoma (PAIS) is a rare and aggressive vascular malignancy whose clinical and radiological features overlap with those of pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE); most patients are initially anticoagulated, and no standard systemic therapy exists for unresectable disease. Amplification of MDM2 is the defining genomic event, yet it is usually treated as a supplementary finding rather than as a diagnostic test. Case presentation A 51-year-old man without thromboembolic risk factors presented with cough, sputum production, and chest discomfort. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed filling defects extending from the main pulmonary artery into both branches together with a 5.0 × 2.7 cm left upper lobe mass, and he received rivaroxaban until hemoptysis occurred. 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET)/CT showed concordant hypermetabolism of the intravascular and parenchymal lesions. Two biopsies, including an expert review, narrowed the differential only to intimal sarcoma versus sarcomatoid carcinoma; next-generation sequencing then identified MDM2 amplification with CDKN2A deletion, a low tumor mutational burden (1.95 mutations/Mb), and negative PD-L1 expression, establishing MDM2-driven PAIS. Because the tumor was unresectable, he received six cycles of sintilimab, docetaxel, and cisplatin, two further cycles of sintilimab and docetaxel, consolidative intensity-modulated radiotherapy (60 Gy in 25 fractions), and maintenance sintilimab monotherapy. The best response was stable disease with a 27.9% reduction in the sum of target-lesion diameters, and progression-free survival reached 12.1 months without grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events. Conclusions When morphology and immunohistochemistry are indeterminate, MDM2 amplification can be the decisive diagnostic test rather than a supplementary finding, and it should be sought before empirical treatment is committed. Chemotherapy-primed PD-1 blockade followed by consolidative radiotherapy produced durable disease control in an immunologically cold tumor; prospective registries are needed to test this sequence.

title: Splenic Abscess Masquerading as Left Lobar Pneumonia: Early Detection with Point-of- Care Ultrasound in the Emergency Department – a case report
abstract: Abstract Splenic abscess is a rare but potentially life-threatening intra-abdominal infection that often presents with nonspecific symptoms, leading to frequent misdiagnosis and delayed treatment. Thoracoabdominal pain, particularly on the left side, may mimic respiratory conditions such as pneumonia. We report a case of a 22-year-old male who presented with one week of left-sided chest and upper abdominal pain, low-grade fever, and anorexia. He was initially treated as having left lobar pneumonia. However, bedside point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) performed in the emergency department revealed a wedge-shaped hypoechoic lesion in the spleen, prompting further investigation. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed a large subcapsular splenic abscess with mass effect on adjacent organs. Laboratory studies showed marked leukocytosis (WBC 28 ×10³/µL) with left shift and elevated ESR (120 mm/hr). Transthoracic echocardiography showed no vegetations. The patient was managed with abscess drainage, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, later tailored to culture and sensitivity. The patient was symptom-free during follow-up with normal investigations and no residual collection. title: Benefits of thyroid screening and evidence suggesting radiation exposure as a cause of increased pediatric thyroid cancer in Fukushima Prefecture
abstract: Abstract The Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident released a large quantity of radioactive materials, including radioactive iodine, which can cause thyroid cancer. Following the accident, Fukushima Prefecture conducted thyroid ultrasound examinations (TUEs) among approximately 380,000 individuals aged 18 years or younger or in utero at the time of the accident. The thyroid cancer (TC) incidence detected through this program was several dozen times higher than the national average, raising concerns regarding screening effects, overdiagnosis, and whether to reduce or discontinue the program. However, the clinical benefits of TUEs remain unclear. Using data from the NPO 311Fund, which supports patients inside and outside Fukushima, we evaluated the clinical implications of screening. Compared with patients diagnosed clinically after symptomatic presentation, those identified through screening exhibited approximately one-fifth the total thyroidectomy rate, one-sixth the rate of distant metastasis, and 40% of the radioiodine therapy rate. Furthermore, a strong positive correlation was observed between regional radiation dose estimates and TC incidence (R² = 0.9723, p = 0.014). This correlation, combined with the increasing proportion of male cases, suggests that radiation exposure is a causal factor for the observed increase in thyroid cancer in this population.

title: Preoperative Bone Marrow Lesion Severity and Early Quality of Recovery After Medial Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background The prognostic significance of preoperative bone marrow lesions (BMLs) after medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) remains uncertain. This study investigated the association between preoperative medial BML severity and early postoperative quality of recovery. Methods This single-centre retrospective cohort study included 173 patients who underwent medial UKA between December 2024 and August 2025. Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging was used to calculate a composite medial BML score ranging from 0 to 6. Patients were classified into no-BML (n = 36), mild (n = 60), moderate (n = 42), and severe (n = 35) groups. The primary outcome was the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at discharge. Secondary outcomes included postoperative pain area under the curve (AUC), knee circumference change, and Knee Society Scores (KSS) at 3, 6, and 12 months. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation and multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors. False discovery rate (FDR) adjustment across 20 outcomes was performed as a sensitivity analysis. Results Mean discharge QoR-15 scores were 134.92 ± 6.87, 132.98 ± 6.70, 130.62 ± 8.76, and 130.17 ± 9.14 across increasing BML severity groups (P = 0.031). After covariate adjustment, each one-point increase in BML score was associated with a 0.755-point decrease in QoR-15 (95% CI − 1.384 to − 0.125; P = 0.019) and a 0.125-cm increase in postoperative knee circumference change (95% CI 0.010–0.241; P = 0.034). Neither association remained statistically significant after FDR adjustment (q = 0.125 and q = 0.169, respectively). No clear associations were observed with postoperative pain AUC or KSS during the first postoperative year. Conclusions Greater preoperative medial BML severity showed nominal associations with poorer early recovery quality and greater postoperative knee swelling, although these findings did not remain statistically significant after multiplicity adjustment. By examining discharge QoR-15 rather than solely knee-specific outcomes, this study addresses a less-explored dimension of recovery after medial UKA. Further prospective validation is required before medial BML severity can be used as an independent prognostic indicator.

title: Parameter-Efficient Mask-Conditioned Magnetic Resonance Image Synthesis for Segmentation Augmentation
abstract: Abstract When real training images for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation are limited, existing masks can be reused to synthesize additional image appearances. However, paired image-translation methods may favor pixel fidelity over distributional similarity, while full diffusion-model fine-tuning is costly and generic conditioning does not explicitly encode mask geometry. To address these limitations, we propose ControlNet-guided Low-Rank Adaptation for MRI synthesis (\method), a mask-conditioned latent diffusion framework that adapts both the denoising and spatial-conditioning pathways. Only 2.96\% of the framework parameters are trainable in the BraTS configuration. We evaluate image quality and segmentation utility on BraTS2020 brain MRI and ACDC cardiac MRI across four fractions of real training slices. On BraTS T1 contrast-enhanced MRI, \method achieves a lower FID than Pix2Pix (55.65 versus 162.42), although Pix2Pix has higher paired pixel fidelity. With 10\% real training slices, adding synthetic pairs raises mean Dice from 0.7208 to 0.7401 and reduces HD95 from 48.43 to 45.34 pixels in a within-cohort, slice-level BraTS evaluation. On 50 held-out ACDC patients, a separately trained adapter raises mean Dice from 0.7661 to 0.8263 and reduces HD95 from 15.40 to 13.63 pixels at the same fraction. Gains diminish as real-image availability increases. These results support targeted use of parameter-efficient, mask-conditioned MRI synthesis when real-image coverage is low.

title: Interpretable multimodal deep learning for diagnosis and symptom-onset prediction in genetic frontotemporal dementia
abstract: Abstract Background: Genetic frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is characterized by substantial clinical and neuroanatomical heterogeneity, making prediction of symptom onset challenging. We evaluated whether deep learning-derived MRI biomarkers could be combined with non-imaging biomarkers in an interpretable framework for diagnosis and phenoconversion prediction in genetic FTD. Methods: We evaluated Multi-ICNN, a multimodal extension of the Interpretable Convolutional Neural Network, using data from the FTD Risk Cohort. Imaging biomarkers derived from T1-weighted MRI were combined with demographic, genetic, and neuropsychological biomarkers in an additive prediction model. We evaluated classification of symptomatic mutation carriers versus genetically confirmed non-carriers and phenoconversion prediction within 2- and 5-year time horizons. Biomarker contributions were examined at the group and participant levels. Results: For diagnosis, Multi-ICNN achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.953, numerically outperforming the single-modality models. For phenoconversion prediction, the deep learning-based models outperformed the conventional volumetric and non-imaging models. The imaging-only ICNN achieved the highest mean AUCs of 0.798 and 0.780 for the 2- and 5-year horizons, respectively. Adding non-imaging biomarkers did not further improve ICNN performance. Neuropsychological measures contributed most strongly to diagnosis, whereas imaging-derived biomarkers dominated phenoconversion prediction, particularly biomarkers involving frontal and temporal regions. The additive model also provided participant-specific biomarker contributions. Conclusions: Interpretable deep learning-derived MRI biomarkers showed promise for phenoconversion prediction in genetic FTD, while the value of multimodal integration depended on the clinical task. The main limitations were the modest sample size and lack of external validation, reflecting the rarity of genetic FTD and the limited availability of comparable longitudinal cohorts.

title: Deep Generative Models Meet Federated Learning: A Healthcare-Centered Review
abstract: Abstract The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare holds significant promise, yet remains constrained by data scarcity, privacy and ethical concerns, and the inherent complexity of medical tasks. This review explores the intersection of deep generative modeling and federated learning, two complementary paradigms that enable collaborative and privacy-preserving innovation. We survey a total of 85 articles on recent trends in deep generative models for healthcare, with a special focus on federated settings. The review is structured around model architectures, providing a taxonomy-driven analysis that emphasizes solutions tailored to the heterogeneity of healthcare data. The current literature is largely limited to single-modality models; multimodal frameworks have only emerged over the last three years of our 7-year scope ($n=14$), where they are beginning to gain traction. Among deep generative approaches, generative adversarial networks dominate the field, particularly in medical image synthesis, where they comprise 66\% of the studies. While alternative architectures such as variational autoencoders remain marginally represented in federated healthcare scenarios, diffusion and autoregressive models are gaining importance, suggesting a paradigm shift in the near future. Notably, the number of related publications has increased substantially in recent years, rising from 1 in 2020 to as many as 31 in 2025, with 2026 pointing toward a similar trend, reflecting the growing interest and momentum in this area. This paper highlights key challenges, open research questions, and future directions for the development of robust, distributed generative AI in healthcare.

title: MEFV Genetic Variants and Acute Abdominal Presentations in Adults Undergoing Genetic Testing for Familial Mediterranean Fever: A Retrospective Single-Center Study
abstract: Abstract Background Familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) is an inherited autoinflammatory disease characterized by recurrent attacks of fever and serosal inflammation. The relationship between MEFV genetic characteristics and acute abdominal outcomes remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations between MEFV variants and emergency department presentations, abdominal computed tomography (CT) abnormalities, and surgical intervention in adults with detected MEFV variants. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 171 adults with at least one detected MEFV variant who underwent MEFV testing between January 1, 2021 and December 31, 2024. Demographic characteristics, MEFV variant number and type, zygosity, ACMG classification, emergency department presentations for abdominal pain, abdominal CT findings, and surgical intervention were retrospectively assessed. Group comparisons used parametric, nonparametric, and exact tests as appropriate (p < 0.05). Results Among 171 patients, 66.7% were female; mean age was 37.99 ± 14.13 years. One MEFV variant was detected in 129 patients (75.4%), two variants in 41 (24.0%), and four variants in one patient (0.6%). M694V was the most frequent single variant. Sixty-five patients (38.0%) presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain during the study period. Fourteen patients (8.2%) had abdominal CT abnormalities. All patients with CT abnormalities presented to the emergency department, versus 32.5% of those without ( p = 0.001). Surgical intervention was performed in four patients (2.3%). Surgery was more frequent with CT abnormalities (14.3% vs 1.3%; p = 0.025). All four patients who underwent surgery had an emergency department presentation ( p = 0.005), and the number of emergency department visits was higher in the surgical group ( p = 0.028). Specific MEFV variants were not significantly associated with emergency department presentation or surgical intervention. Conclusions Specific MEFV variants and the number of detected variants were not significantly associated with emergency department utilization or surgical intervention in this cohort. In contrast, abdominal CT abnormalities were associated with emergency department presentations and were associated with a higher frequency of surgical intervention. Larger prospective studies are warranted.

title: Can Intrapartum Ultrasound At 6-Cm Cervical Dilatation Predict Time To Delivery In Nulliparous Women? A Prospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Objective To investigate whether intrapartum ultrasonography performed at 6-cm cervical dilatation can provide early prediction of time to delivery in nulliparous women and to identify the most clinically useful ultrasound parameter for this purpose. Methods This prospective cohort study included 57 nulliparous women with singleton, cephalic pregnancies in the active phase of labor. After confirmation of 6-cm cervical dilatation and ruptured membranes, intrapartum ultrasound was performed using transperineal and transabdominal approaches. Transperineal ultrasound was used to measure the angle of progression (AoP), head–perineum distance (HPD), and midline angle (MLA), while transabdominal ultrasound assessed fetal head orientation and occiput position. The primary outcome was the interval between ultrasound assessment and delivery. Maternal, fetal, and labor-related characteristics were prospectively recorded. Statistical analyses included Mann–Whitney U, Kruskal–Wallis, Spearman correlation, multivariable linear regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses to evaluate the predictive performance of AoP and HPD for delivery within 1, 2, and 4 hours. Statistical significance was defined as P <.05. Results Among all intrapartum ultrasound parameters, AoP demonstrated the strongest overall predictive performance for time to delivery. AoP showed a significant negative correlation with time to delivery, whereas HPD demonstrated a significant positive correlation. ROC analysis demonstrated that AoP had moderate predictive performance for delivery within 2 hours (AUC = 0.692), with an optimal cutoff of ≥ 124.5° (sensitivity 62.5%, PPV 65.2%), and good predictive performance for delivery within 4 hours (AUC = 0.761), with a cutoff of ≥ 119.5° (sensitivity 65.2%, PPV 93.8%). HPD showed moderate predictive performance for delivery within 1 hour (AUC = 0.697); no woman with an HPD > 39.5 mm delivered within the first hour. Head station was the strongest independent predictor (β = 0.258; p = 0.017), with significantly higher delivery rate within 2 hours when station was ≥ + 1 (p < 0.001). Occiput anterior and upward head direction were associated with shorter labor, whereas prolonged labor correlated with lower Apgar scores. MLA showed no significant predictive value. Conclusion In nulliparous women, intrapartum ultrasound performed at the onset of the active phase of labor provides objective parameters for predicting time to delivery. Although fetal head station was the strongest independent predictor, AoP was the most clinically applicable ultrasound parameter because it provided objective prediction of delivery within 2–4 hours early in the active phase of labor, whereas HPD was particularly useful for excluding delivery within the first hour. Our findings suggest that intrapartum AoP assessment at the onset of active labor enables clinically meaningful prediction of delivery time several hours before the second stage of labor, extending the role of intrapartum ultrasound beyond assessment of labor progress to early prognostic decision-making.
